32a06b566f7d9952: PETALING JAYA: A total of 70,195 undocumented migrants were detained in 11,808 enforcement operations conducted by the Immigration Department nationwide between Jan 1 and Oct 31.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 155,498 people were inspected during the same period, while 328,744 registered under the Migrant Repatriation Programme 2.0.
Of those registered, 243,501 had returned to their home countries through the programme.
"During the same period, 52,585 undocumented migrants were deported after completing the legal and documentation processes," he said.

Zakaria said the department continued to take enforcement action against foreigners who breached immigration regulations, including overstaying, misusing passes or staying in the country without valid documents.
He said operations were targeted at high-risk areas where immigration offences were likely to occur, including residential areas, workplaces, business premises and locations frequented by foreigners.

Monitoring also focused on various methods used to breach immigration regulations, including misuse of pass facilities, the use of premises for accommodation or transit, and the illegal employment of foreigners.s
"Information gathered through surveillance and cooperation with other agencies helps the department identify those suspected of breaching immigration laws and plan enforcement operations," he said.
The department also conducted operations jointly with other enforcement agencies, including the police, National Registration Department and local authorities.S
662a534d98a7567c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Taiwanese actress Vivian Sung is no stranger to taking on different roles, but her latest film presented a challenge that required her to immerse herself in Malaysian daily life.
In the Malaysian-Taiwanese production The Age of Goodbyes, Sung plays Du Li An, whose story unfolds against the historical backdrop of Ipoh.
In an interview with Malay Mail she mentioned her biggest challenge was mastering the Malaysian Mandarin accent, which she worked on extensively before filming.
Besides working with an acting coach to practise her lines, Sung immersed herself in everyday Malaysian life to become more familiar with how locals spoke.
“I moved to Kuala Lumpur a month before filming.
“Every day, I went outside to markets and shops to talk to local people.
“I tried having casual conversations with them to practise,” she said.
She even tested her progress by seeing whether locals could recognise her Taiwanese roots when she spoke in a Malaysian accent.
However, her attempts did not always go as planned, as many people quickly identified her as Taiwanese, much to her disappointment.
Despite this, she persisted with her daily conversations and gradually became more comfortable with the accent over the course of the month.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The cast of ‘The Age of Goodbyes’ attended the film's premiere screening at GSC LaLaport BBCC on November 12. — Picture courtesy of Mega Films Distribution
Although Sung had visited Malaysia several times before, her previous trips were mostly for film promotions, which usually lasted only a day or two.
Working on The Age of Goodbyes gave her the opportunity to experience the country beyond the usual tourist attractions and brief promotional visits.
She also spent a month in Ipoh, where most of the film was shot.
“I felt Malaysia was so beautiful, especially Ipoh.
“The nature and lakes were wonderful, and I had a great experience filming here.”
Sung also praised the professionalism of the Malaysian actors and spoke fondly of the local dishes she had the opportunity to try during her stay in Ipoh.
Directed by Edmund Yeo, The Age of Goodbyes also marks a rare foray into art-house cinema for Sung, who has previously appeared mainly in leading roles in youth romances and romantic comedies.
What drew her to the role of Du Li An was the character’s charm, emotional struggles and transformation from a young woman into adulthood, as well as the film’s Malaysian historical backdrop.
“I just felt that Du Li An was such a charming character.
“When I read the script, I knew I had to play her.”
The film is adapted from a novel by Li Zi Shu, which Sung read approximately six times before filming.
Each reading gave her a different perspective on the character and the story.
She said she was surprised and fascinated not only by Du Li An but also by the wider storyline and its 1960s setting.
Although she had never experienced that era herself, the novel introduced her to numerous stories that she felt were worth sharing with audiences through the film.
Sung, who has watched the film three times, said each viewing offered her different lessons and perspectives.
“Every time I watched the movie, I took away different lessons myself.
“I hope audiences will understand through this movie that no matter what happens in life, no matter how difficult things may be, we all have choices.
“I hope we can bring love into our lives and turn our vulnerabilities into strength,” she said.
The Age of Goodbyes is now showing in Malaysian cinemas.
44c28b272b602e54: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 63-year-old retiree lost RM80,000 after falling victim to a non-existent online investment scheme promoted through WhatsApp.
District police chief assistant commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim joined the scheme earlier this month after being introduced to it by an acquaintance.
He said the victim was lured by promises of substantial returns within a short period.
"Initially, the victim invested RM93,525 from his retirement savings and received a return of RM18,000 on Nov 11.

"Encouraged by the profit, he made three further transactions totalling RM80,000 on Nov 12. However, he did not receive any returns and was told that his investment had yet to reach the RM100,000 threshold," he said.
He said the victim realised he had been cheated when he was instructed to make an additional payment of RM50,000 to access the promised profits.
He said the victim lodged a police report at 6.20pm yesterday, adding that police were investigating the case under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The offence carries a maximum penalty of 10 years' jail, and whipping.
fe03548ff92f4cdd: KUALA LUMPUR: Interim coach Tan Cheng Hoe blamed the two early goals for Harimau Malaya's 2-0 defeat to China in a friendly in Guangdong on Saturday.
Playing at the Zhaoqing New District Sports Centre, the world No. 96 hosts took the lead in the 10th minute through a Wang Yudong header before Zhang Yuning doubled the advantage nine minutes later.
Cheng Hoe said the setback forced his team to make several changes to their game plan.
"I am certainly disappointed with this result because we conceded two goals, especially the early goal in the opening 10 minutes, which put us in a difficult situation to bounce back.
"In football, it becomes very difficult when you fall two goals behind early in the game because you have to change several things in the team," he said at a post-match press conference.

Despite the result, which extended Malaysia's 46-year winless run against China since 1980, the 58-year-old praised his players for a stronger second-half display after introducing Haziq Kutty Abba and Richard Chin.

"We brought on two players, Haziq and Richard. We tried to play with a more attacking approach because we needed an early goal in the second half to boost confidence before trying to get an equaliser.
"In the second half, we played much better. We controlled the ball well and created more chances," he said.
Harimau Malaya thought they had reduced the deficit in the 77th minute when Fergus Tierney fired a shot from outside the box into the net.
However, their celebrations were cut short after a VAR review ruled out the goal following a foul by Safwan Mazlan earlier in the attacking move.
Tierney's difficult evening ended with a red card in the 90th minute after he received a second booking for retaliating following a foul by Alex Yang.
World No. 133 Malaysia will next face 144th-ranked Yemen in another friendly at the same venue on Tuesday.
6c76e89c77a1e7f5: STARBASE, Nov 15 — Elon Musk’s SpaceX yesterday pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat that shows the feasibility of fully reusable rockets and brings affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality.

The Starship emerged from a cloudy sky after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2.

The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible.
“That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said.

Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the nerve-wracking final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream.
It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system.
The Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.

Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude compared to boosters.
Musk congratulated the SpaceX team and posted videos of the spaceship hanging between the chopstick arms, saying the vessel “looks great!”

Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.”
“Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added.
Analyst Kathleen Curlee hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done.

“What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability... to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” said Curlee, of Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.
‘Giant swoosh’
Starship’s path home had been carefully mapped out to avoid population centres as it travelled over the continent, said senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore.

Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh manoeuvre” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east.
Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centres into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars.
US space agency Nasa is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. Yesterday, Administrator Jared Isaacman called the spaceship recovery “almost magic.”
“Making more believers by the day... one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X.
Musk envisions Starship as being the workhorse of “rapidly reusable” rockets, with a goal of hourly launches that could send things like internet satellites and data centres into space.
Refuelling challenge

Musk, the world’s richest person, has already revolutionised the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which regularly launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station.

But the Starship project has been plagued by delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges, including the unsolved problem of transferring fuel to the spaceship while in orbit — a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars.

It will also need to further fine-tune the Super Heavy booster, which ran into a technical issue Friday on its descent, forcing a diversion to the Gulf of Mexico. It, too, was supposed to have been caught by the “chopstick arms.”
Following SpaceX’s high-profile stock market debut in June that raised about US$85.7 billion, the company is investing heavily in production and launch capabilities.

During a tour of its million-square-foot (93,000-square-metre) factory at Starbase on Friday, SpaceX officials told journalists it now has the capability to produce a spaceship every two weeks and a booster every four weeks. — AFP
079504fc56d43309: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 15 — A man was shot dead, believed to have been killed by a colleague, at an oil storage depot in Bukit Tengah here yesterday.

Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted by Bernama yesterday, confirmed the incident and said the suspect fled the scene after the shooting, with police actively searching for him.
“Further investigations are underway, and police are investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder,” he said.
Lim said the victim’s body had been sent to hospital for a post-mortem examination.
It is learnt that the incident occurred at about 4.30pm, when the 41-year-old victim was believed to have been shot three times by the suspect, who is in his 40s. — Bernama
d08771f64652611a: KUALA LUMPUR: A large number of children took part in a gut health awareness programme organised by GK Bio International Sdn Bhd (GKB), earning the company a place in the Malaysia Book of Records.
The achievement was recognised under the category 'Largest Children Participation in Gut Health Awareness Programme'.
The record was set during Zoo Builders, a five-day interactive educational event held from Nov 5 to 9 at Sunway Pyramid, Selangor.
The initiative reflects GKB's commitment to promoting preventive healthcare and encouraging healthier lifestyle habits from an early age.
HANDS-ON LEARNING
Through interactive learning stations, children were introduced to the importance of maintaining good digestive health, making balanced food choices and drinking sufficient water every day.
One of the main attractions was the Builder Base station, which served as the official participation checkpoint for the Malaysia Book of Records achievement.

At the station, children selected their usual daily water intake levels before taking part in a food selection activity. They then created their own meal plates using food props based on their eating habits.

GKB consultants introduced the Health Ministry's Suku-Suku Separuh concept, which encourages balanced meals comprising one-quarter grains or carbohydrates, one-quarter protein and half vegetables and fruits.
The children were also introduced to the Bristol Stool Chart through age-appropriate explanations. This helped them understand how stool appearance can provide useful clues about digestive health.
The activities were designed to turn health information into practical lessons that children could understand and apply in their daily lives.
Beyond the educational component, Zoo Builders featured three other activity stations.

These included Builder Supply Point, where families could explore GKB's health and wellness products; Builder Portrait, a dedicated photo area; and Builder Reward, where children who completed the activities could collect complimentary tokens and take part in lucky spin and gashapon games.
ENCOURAGING HEALTHIER HABITS
GKB said the initiative was part of its broader effort to bridge the gap between scientific health knowledge and everyday living.
The company believes that developing an understanding of gut health during childhood can help children adopt healthier habits as they grow older.
As a science-driven health and wellness company, GKB specialises in probiotics, medicinal fungi, functional ingredients and innovative health solutions.
It is supported by more than 150 research and development professionals, including food technologists, pharmacists and dietitians, and offers more than 30 product lines.
Its products are distributed through more than 3,000 retail outlets, hospitals and clinics nationwide. The company also has an expanding presence in Singapore and Brunei.
Through initiatives such as Zoo Builders, GKB aims to encourage families to take a more proactive approach to preventive healthcare.
The programme reinforces the importance of balanced nutrition, adequate hydration and everyday wellness.

f62b6fdeb41c032d: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) culled 2,782 pigeons and crows last month to curb pest nuisances and maintain public hygiene.
MBPP said 1,035 pigeons were captured while 1,747 crows were culled during ongoing population control operations.
It also destroyed 36 crow nests to curb breeding and reduce safety risks, particularly in residential areas and commercial hubs.

"To deter public feeding, which contributes to population surges, we also issued seven compounds under Section 47(1)(g) of the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974," it said in a Facebook statement.
MBPP reminded the public not to feed pigeons and crows in public spaces, as this attracts flocks, accelerates breeding and causes environmental pollution through droppings and food waste.
The city council also advised residents and businesses to dispose of food waste properly and keep their surroundings clean.
A total of 14,185 crows and 12,004 pigeons were culled at identified hotspots between January and September.
In 2025, MBPP culled 17,750 crows and captured 10,171 pigeons.
87093ebbf8d7d6f9: MELAKA: Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to be sworn in as chief minister today.
BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured enough seats to form the state government in yesterday's 16th Melaka state election.
The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place at 11am at the Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri's office, paving the way for Rauf to continue leading the state for a second term.
The BN-PN cooperation secured 24 of the 28 state seats contested, giving it a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
BN won 21 seats, while PN secured three.
Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that the alliance would nominate Ab Rauf to continue leading the state government following its victory in the election.
Rauf secured a more convincing victory in defending the Tanjung Bidara seat, winning by a majority of 8,615 votes compared with just 364 votes in the 15th Melaka state election in 2021.
He defeated Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri in a straight fight.

In the 2021 state election, Rauf won Tanjung Bidara in a three-cornered contest with 3,559 votes, defeating PN candidate Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin, who received 3,195 votes, and PH candidate Zainal Hassan, who garnered 489 votes.
Rauf was appointed Melaka's 13th chief minister on March 31, 2023, replacing Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali, who resigned.
22099a71e16871fa: KUALA LUMPUR: Rohingya refugees, cybercrime, haze and public health, including youth mental health, are among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat next week.

According to the Order Paper published on Parliament's official website, Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong) will ask the Home Ministry for the latest number of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia and how many were repatriated to Myanmar this year.
He also wants the government to explain how the Rohingya refugees entered Malaysia and which agencies are responsible for the lapses that allowed their entry.

Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PH-Balik Pulau) will ask the home minister to outline the government's long-term mechanisms for managing Rohingya refugees still in Malaysia following the suspension of third-country resettlement efforts.
This includes resettlement targets and cooperation with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and third countries.

On the same issue, Azahari Hasan (PN-Padang Rengas) will ask the home minister about the Home Ministry's monitoring and enforcement mechanisms for the Rohingya community in Malaysia to ensure refugee status is not misused to commit crimes or engage in activities that threaten public safety.

Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob (BN-Bera) will seek details on the government's long-term strategy for managing refugees and asylum seekers, as well as the extent to which the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) can ensure their identities are verified and their status, security and whereabouts in the country are monitored.

The Home Ministry will also be asked by Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar) to provide an update on the comprehensive digital mapping of the Malaysia-Thailand border in Perlis, including the identification of illegal crossing routes, high-risk areas, security gaps and locations requiring immediate security intervention.
He also wants to know whether the government has an integrated geospatial database that can be accessed under controlled conditions.

Meanwhile, Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) will ask the home minister about measures to strengthen the police force in terms of the number and expertise of investigators, technology, digital forensics, as well as the powers and resources needed to tackle increasingly complex crimes.
These include cybercrime, financial fraud, organised crime and cases requiring digital forensic evidence.

Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan (PN-Permatang Pauh) will seek an explanation from the home minister on the causes of online scam losses reaching RM3.8 billion, the low rate of fund recovery for victims and efforts to rescue Malaysians who have fallen victim to fake job offers overseas.
Mohd Hasnizan Harun (PN-Hulu Selangor) will also ask the home minister for the number of online scam cases and losses recorded so far in 2026.

He also wants the government to outline the Home Ministry's plans to introduce liability principles that would hold banks, telecommunications companies and digital platforms accountable when weaknesses in their systems contribute to scams.
The Health Ministry will also come under scrutiny during this week's Dewan Rakyat sitting, with several questions on the country's public health challenges expected to be raised.

Datuk Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (PN-Tanjong Karang) will ask the health minister when the government plans to introduce a sustainable national health financing framework to reduce the public healthcare system's reliance on annual allocations and address rising treatment costs.
48805c85f488c6c9: SANDAKAN, Nov 15 — The Social Security Organisation (Socso) has disbursed RM20.23 million in benefits under the Non-Occupational Accident Scheme (Lindung 24 Jam) to contributors and their dependants as of Oct 31.

Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the amount involved 12,582 eligible contributors and dependants who received various income-replacement benefits under Lindung 24 Jam to ensure their socioeconomic well-being in times of adversity.

“A total of 373 recipients from Sabah received benefits amounting to more than RM481,000. Lindung 24 Jam demonstrates how the scheme serves as a form of protection to ensure that workers and their families receive financial support in the event of an accident.

“Therefore, I urge all workers, particularly in Sabah, to ensure that their coverage under the scheme remains active. Contributors who previously opted out are encouraged to rejoin the scheme,” he said in a statement issued in conjunction with the Kenduri Rakyat i Lindung u @ Batu Sapi programme here yesterday.

Khairul Firdaus also said that, apart from efforts to stimulate the labour market, the provision of the Mobility Assistance Allowance (EBM), which came into effect on Oct 1, had begun benefiting its target groups.

He said the latest benefit, introduced following amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800), had seen the disbursement of allocations amounting to RM12,000 involving 12 eligible recipients, serving as a catalyst for career transitions in an increasingly dynamic labour market.

“We want every career transition opportunity to be fully accessible without geographical limitations, as the government understands that various factors are taken into consideration when evaluating job offers. Therefore, the EBM will provide the best possible benefits to insured persons under Act 800, including the younger generation in Sabah,” he said.

On today’s programme, Khairul Firdaus said the outreach initiative reflected the Madani Government’s commitment to ensuring that social protection benefits reached the people directly, regardless of their background, occupation or location, including those in rural and remote areas of Sabah.

He said the programme also enabled the public to obtain information, advice and Socso services directly at the counters provided, alongside various services offered by several departments, including the Sabah Labour Department, Department of Occupational Safety and Health, and Manpower Department. — Bernama
a439cbbadf38db19: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) is well-positioned to benefit from growing demand for advanced power semiconductor packaging, supported by the strong growth outlook of German chipmaker Infineon Technologies AG.

CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said MPI had invested about US$65 million in its financial year ended 2026 (FY26) to expand its artificial intelligence (AI) server-related packaging capabilities and increase production capacity for new power modules at its Carsem facility in Ipoh.
Infineon's AI data centre power revenue more than doubled to over €1.7 billion in FY26 from €700 million a year earlier, exceeding its earlier guidance of €1.5 billion.
The growth was driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments, production capacity expansion and higher power semiconductor content per AI server.
Infineon expects its combined AI and conventional data centre power revenue to reach nearly €4 billion in FY27.

CIMB Securities said the outlook was supported by multi-year customer supply and capacity reservation arrangements, both signed and under negotiation, which could underpin more than €10 billion in potential cumulative revenue.

"We believe Infineon's strong growth trajectory is a positive read-through for MPI, which is well-positioned to benefit from rising demand for advanced power semiconductor packaging," it said in a research note.
The firm expects the new power modules to increase MPI's AI-related revenue contribution from 13 per cent in FY26 to 18 per cent in FY27 and 23 per cent in FY28.
It said MPI is also expected to ramp up production of new vertical power delivery-enabled modules in FY27, providing another growth avenue through higher packaging content value.

"Over the medium term, we expect the growing adoption of 800 volt data centre server-rack architectures to accelerate demand for wide-bandgap power solutions, particularly silicon carbide and gallium nitride, creating further opportunities for MPI to capture higher semiconductor packaging content per AI server," it said.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on MPI but lowered its target price to RM48.50 from its previous valuation.
The revised target price is based on a lower price-to-earnings multiple of 29 times, compared with 37 times previously, while rolling forward its valuation to end in 2027.
CIMB Securities said the lower valuation reflected weaker global technology sentiment amid inflationary pressures and concerns over a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure investment.
13a9889b99fbb9e7: KUALA KANGSAR: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced the Pledge of Loyalty and Investiture Ceremony held in conjunction with his 70th birthday at Istana Iskandariah.
Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad was also present.

Earlier, Sultan Nazrin inspected a guard of honour comprising 103 members and three officers from the Royal Army Engineers Regiment 2 Division, based at Sangro Camp, Taiping, led by Colonel Abdul Rahim Hamzah.
The guard of honour was headed by Major Mohd Izuan Mohamed, with Warrant Officer 1 Mohamad Fairus Nizam Zabory serving as parade sergeant major.
A 21-gun salute was fired by the 41st Battery of the Royal Artillery Regiment, based at Sungai Buluh Camp, Selangor, and led by Lieutenant Colonel Hafizan Mat Ghani.
Sultan Nazrin conferred state awards and medals on 218 recipients during the first ceremonial session today, while the second session will be held on Nov 21.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry secretary-general Datuk Anis Rizana Mohd Zainudin heads the list of recipients.
Anis Rizana, a former Customs Department director-general, will receive the Darjah Seri Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk Seri.

Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman will receive the Darjah Datuk Seri Panglima Taming Sari, which also carries the title Datuk Seri, while Accountant-General Nasran Omar will receive the Darjah Datuk Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini, which carries the title Datuk.

The Darjah Datuk Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk, will be conferred on 14 recipients, including state executive council member Sandrea Ng Shy Ching, Ipoh Mayor Zamakhshari Hanipah and Bernama editor-in-chief D.R. Arul Rajoo.
Eight recipients, including Perak deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Azlin Sadari, will receive the Darjah Datuk Pahlawan Taming Sari, which carries the title Datuk Pahlawan.

The other awards comprise the Darjah Ahli Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini for 10 recipients, Darjah Ahli Paduka Mahkota Perak for 28, Darjah Ahli Cura Si Manja Kini (ACM) for 18 and Darjah Ahli Mahkota Perak for 47.
Bernama Perak bureau chief Syamsiah Sahat will be among the ACM recipients.
The state will also confer the Pingat Pekerti Terpilih on 49 recipients, Pingat Jasa Kebaktian on 31 and Pingat Lama Perkhidmatan on 10.
f3ede4a16029e0ba: ANTALYA, Nov 15 — Thousands of protesters took to the streets yesterday in the Turkish city hosting COP31 to accuse the climate summit of failing those bearing the brunt of environmental destruction.
The show of dissent comes as negotiators approach the crunch final week of global climate talks in Antalya, with nearly 200 nations scrambling to strike a deal by Friday.

The summit is not expected to produce a major breakthrough, frustrating activists demanding tougher curbs on planet-warming fossil fuels and fresh pledges to help poorer countries adapt to climate impacts.

In downtown Antalya, under rainy skies, thousands of protesters dressed in costumes and shouting slogans marched under close police supervision in the largest demonstration since COP31 began on tomorrow.
“We are suffering the consequences of climate injustice, yet our voices are never heard at the COP,” said Halime Saman from the People’s Climate Summit platform, one of the groups behind the rally.
“Turkey is the co-chair of COP31 but still has no roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. New power stations and coal mines are being opened,” she told AFP.
Yasar Gokoglu, a 78-year-old demonstrator, travelled nearly 600 kilometres (350 miles) from Adana in southern Turkey to denounce what he called “a masquerade sponsored by monopolies”.
Police estimated that more than 7,000 people attended the protest, which was organised by environmental groups, trade unions and rights organisations, and proceeded without any major incident.
Civil society activists had raised safety concerns ahead of COP31 after Turkey embarked on a major crackdown on the Muslim-majority country’s LGBT community in September.
Some LGBT protesters waving rainbow flags participated in the march.
Demonstrators were only allowed to join the rally after being searched by police.

Much smaller demonstrations inside the COP31 venue this week, including one attended by Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, have been mounting pressure on political leaders to act faster on the climate crisis.

The negotiations hit the halfway point yesterday but countries remain far apart on contentious issues including financing adaptation measures in developing nations, defending climate science, and shifting from fossil fuels to clean energy.
Australia’s climate minister, Chris Bowen, who is chairing the formal negotiations, said there had been “really good and positive conversations” but some issues required more time.
Outside the negotiations, Turkey is urging countries to join a voluntary pledge to raise the share of global final energy demand met by electricity.
The summit, which closes on November 20, takes place against a difficult backdrop, with a conflict-driven energy crisis and geopolitical tensions tempering expectations.
“There’s no climate quick fix. No single COP can magic this crisis away, but each must drive progress,” UN climate chief Simon Stiell told reporters yesterday. — AFP
e88a3c71ae2e02fc: SINGAPORE: Coach Hajime Moriyasu said Japan can become the best in the world after beating Brazil for a second time, as he prepares to step down after eight years in charge.
Japan shocked the five-times world champions 3-2 in a friendly in Singapore on Saturday, with substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scoring an injury-time winner.
The victory came just more than a year after Japan beat Brazil for the first time in a friendly in Tokyo.
Brazil eliminated Japan from this year's World Cup in North America with a 2-1 win in the last 32.
Moriyasu will leave his job after a friendly against Paraguay on Tuesday but he is certain that Japan are on track to become a major football nation.
"The players showed confidence and courage and dug in when they needed to dig in," he said.
"At the World Cup in the future, Japan can absolutely become the world's best."
Moriyasu, Japan's longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa.

But the Asian Football Confederation announced that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to "exceptional circumstances" in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country.
The JFA confirmed on Friday that next week's game would be Moriyasu's last.
"Aiming for wins and growth, I will strive to do my best as I always have," Moriyasu said.
Japan were looking for revenge after a heart-breaking loss to Brazil at the World Cup.
Gabriel Martinelli scored in the 95th minute in Houston to send Brazil through.
Japan midfielder Ao Tanaka, who was in floods of tears after making a late mistake in the World Cup game, said after the win in Singapore that he was "calm but really happy."
"All sorts of things started coming back to me as the game got closer, and of course those frustrating memories were in my head," said the Leeds United midfielder.
Japan took an early 2-0 lead before Brazil hit back through two Vinicius Junior wonder strikes.
Coventry winger Sakamoto won it for Japan in injury time, before Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were sent off for protesting the goal.
The 30-year-old Sakamoto was making his first Japan appearance for five years.
"To come back like this and make a contribution in such a massive match, one we all really wanted to win, gives me so much confidence," said Sakamoto.--AFP

cf5b85c0315ba095: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The government has approved a 99-year lease renewal for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH), with the land premium fixed at a nominal RM1,000, a significant reduction from the earlier estimated premium of approximately RM4.67 million.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, in a Facebook post today, said the decision reflects the Madani government’s commitment to safeguarding Kuala Lumpur’s historical landmarks and ensuring that institutions of heritage significance can continue to serve future generations.

She said the nominal premium was approved following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s commitment to give special consideration to the preservation of the historic building, after visiting the hall during a Chinese New Year celebration on February 17.
Hannah announced the decision at KLSCAH’s 103rd anniversary dinner yesterday.

“When the Prime Minister visited this Hall in February, he asked me to find a solution. I took that instruction seriously, and I am pleased that we have been able to deliver an outcome that recognises the importance of preserving this historic institution,” she said.
Hannah said the Federal Territories Land Committee subsequently approved the surrender and re-alienation of the land for institutional use on September 14, with a lease tenure of up to 99 years.

She said the formal approval letter dated October 1 confirmed the land premium at RM1,000 while the total amount payable under the official land notice is RM5,011, inclusive of the first year’s land rent and administrative charges, with the annual land rent fixed at RM3,151.

“Having been recognised as a National Heritage building since 2007, KLSCAH is an important part of Kuala Lumpur’s history. However, heritage recognition must be accompanied by meaningful efforts to ensure that these buildings are properly maintained and preserved.

“By easing the financial burden associated with the land premium, we hope KLSCAH will be able to channel more of its resources towards maintaining the Hall, preserving its heritage and continuing its work for the community,” she said.
Hannah emphasised that heritage preservation must reflect the diverse history and identity of Kuala Lumpur, adding that efforts to safeguard the city’s heritage should extend across all communities.

In this regard, she highlighted the ongoing efforts by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to study the preservation of traditional Malay villages in Sungai Penchala, including Kampung Palimbayan and Kampung Bukit Lanjan.

“Our city’s history was shaped by many communities, and every community has contributed to the Kuala Lumpur we know today. Preserving this shared heritage is a responsibility we must uphold together,” she said. — Bernama
9ba8490e5fe539bf: ANUGERAH Bintang Popular Berita Harian (ABPBH) has given Malaysians a platform to celebrate their favourite entertainers for nearly four decades.

Carrying the theme 'Kitalah Bintang' (We Are The Stars), the upcoming 38th edition also recognises the growing influence of social media personalities, content creators and sporting figures alongside established artistes.
In its launch at Ombak KLCC recently, ABPBH 38 has 21 categories, with five supplementary awards elevated to the main competition to reflect how digital creators increasingly shape public tastes.
Project director Shamshul Azree Samshir, who is also ʻBerita Harianʼ entertainment and projects senior editor, said the theme honoured people who helped the industry thrive, including the fans.
THE NOMINEES ARE...
The five upgraded categories are Popular Influencer, Popular Athlete, Popular Song, Popular On-Screen Couple for Drama and the Star Style Evolution Daia Award.

Popular Influencer contenders include Khairul Aming, Muay Thai fighter Johan Ghazali (Jojo), Kasih Iris Leona, Puteri Rania, Sam Lim, Pinn Yang, Adrian Mr POV, Ammar Ahyan, sibling duo Amin and Abid, and Qayyum Halid of Chesayang Kitchen.

Popular Athlete brings together footballer Arif Aiman Hanapi, track cyclist Datuk Azizulhasni Awang, sprinter Muhammad Azeem Fahmi, badminton players Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, and Jojo again.

Popular On-Screen Couple for Drama contenders are Amir Ahnaf and Siti Khadijah Halim ('Cinta Dalam Sekam'); Azhan Rani and Noorkhiriah ('Seribu Tahun'); Beto Kusyairy and Nabila Huda ('Gayong'); and Shukri Yahaya and Hannah Delisha ('Andai Itu Takdirnya 2').

Popular Song features tracks such as 'Adek Saye Abe Sore' (Eda Ezrin and Den Manjo), 'Sejambak Bunga' (Ernie Zakri), 'Sayang Orang Sama' (Adira), 'Jodoh Lebaran' (Aisha Retno), 'Telepati' (Aziz Harun), 'Gila Bayang' (Ammar Haikal) and 'P. Ramlee Saloma' (ALPHA).
Nominees for the Star Style Evolution Daia Award include Alvin Chong, Allya Syamimi, Ashraf Anuar, Marissa Dania Hakim, Parisa Ardina, Sara Muzam, Scha Alyahya, Awal Ashaari and Sofea Shra.
Traditional categories continue to feature household names.
Beto Kusyairy, Remy Ishak, Shaheizy Sam and Syafiq Kyle are up for Popular Actor (Film), whereas Maya Karin, Nabila Huda, Scha Alyahya and Mimi Lana are vying for Popular Actress (Film).
Aina Abdul, Ernie Zakri, Mimifly and Shila Amzah are competing for Popular Female Singer.
DESIGNING THE STARS
Beyond nominations, the launch featured the Mini Creators Fiesta, highlighted by a fashion workshop led by celebrated Malaysian designer duo Rizman Ruzaini.
For them, ABPBH represents a milestone, having provided an early platform when they were university students.
Rizman Nordin, 42, recalled how dressing singers, such as Datuk Ziana Zain and Dayang Nurfaizah, helped to put their label on the map.

"ABPBH was one of the platforms that allowed young designers like us to introduce our creations. Although we were still students, we seized the opportunity to showcase our designs and people began recognising us. You could say it was free marketing for us at the time," he said, adding that despite challenges, their mission remains making Rizman Ruzaini an icon of Malaysian fashion.
Wan Mohd Ruzaini Wan Jamil, 42, said international events like the Oscars inspired them to bring that same spirit locally.
For the duo, dressing celebrities goes beyond red-carpet outfits; it is about translating a star's personality into a visual statement built on trust.

"We are proud and grateful that after 20 years, we are still part of ABPBH. This was one of the places where we began. Naturally, we want to continue supporting it," Ruzaini said, emphasising the importance of staying grounded while carrying Malaysian fashion internationally.
Ultimately, ABPBH 38's 'Kitalah Bintang' theme honours both the stars and creative talent behind the scenes.
The Lifetime Achievement Award will also return to honour significant industry contribution.

Officiating at the launch of the awards were ABPBH 38 chairman and ʻBerita Harianʼ group editor Zulkifli Jalil, Daia head of marketing Liew Tien Yee, and TV3 and TV9 senior general manager of content and audience strategy Anida Mohd Tahrim.
Co-sponsored by Daia, with Hot FM and Kool FM as official radio partners, ABPBH 38 is supported by digital platforms including Apa Kes? #BHNakTanya, OHBULAN! and Xtra.
The Top 10 voting period runs from Nov 16 to Dec 6 via the official website.
Registered fans will receive 38 free voting points, with final results are decided by 70 per cent public votes and 30 per cent professional jury scores.
The grand finale takes place on Dec 12 at the Selangor International Trade Centre in Shah Alam, airing live on TV3 and Tonton at 9pm.

59eb3e7488d19099: KYIV, Nov 15 — Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released yesterday, saying his country’s relationship with the Western alliance is “back on the agenda.”
Zelensky also warned of the dangers of Moscow’s push to redraw “influence” in Europe and said the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign.
Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Putin and Zelensky Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough.
Negotiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries would join future talks on ending the war.
In Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries — France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland — to send representatives to the talks.
“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said, adding:
“After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go.”
He said the discussion showed that “Nato is back on the agenda” for Ukraine.
Nato and Washington have not yet commented.

Russia meanwhile continued its bombardment yesterday, with deadly strikes in the eastern city of Pavlohrad and in a village near Zaporizhzhia, which is now just a few dozen kilometres from the front line.
Kyiv seeks guarantees
Zelensky said Kyiv was discussing security guarantees with Western partners and that Ukrainians would ultimately decide whether to accept any deal.
He insisted Ukraine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow’s troops as Russian.
Russia has consistently said Kyiv joining Nato is a red line and in 2022 launched its invasion, saying the West planned to incorporate Ukraine into the alliance.
The Kremlin has also ruled out foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine and wider ceasefires.
But Putin earlier this week proposed a “humanitarian” mission to the eastern town of Kostyantynivka, which Moscow announced it had seized in the summer but where Kyiv says fighting continues.
Zelensky said the proposal was a bid to advance Russian gains in Donetsk. “Their next steps will be our other cities in Donbas,” he said.
Moscow’s troops have inched westwards but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region.
‘First, end the war’
Russia has tried to reframe negotiations on ending the war — Europe’s worst since World War II — into a conversation on the continent’s wider security.
In 2021, before its Ukraine invasion, Moscow issued an ultimatum to the West to pull back Nato troops from eastern Europe.
Moscow’s chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, this week called for a “new, modern Yalta”, drawing criticism from European leaders.
Zelensky warned that any discussion of wider security arrangements should come only after the war has ended.
European leaders have reacted coolly to the proposal for a new security architecture.
“We do not need to discuss that, it already exists,” Germany’s Friedrich Merz said Friday.
French President Emmanuel Macron said yesterday that “those who want to ration aid to Ukraine wish underneath it all to force an unjust peace on it” and, by extension, all of Europe.
“That is the spirit of defeat. That is a recipe for another war. That cannot be France’s position,” Macron said.
“What happens in Ukraine concerns us directly.... Helping Ukraine defend itself is protecting France and the French.”
Donald Trump’s administration has for almost two years tried to reach a breakthrough in talks between Russia and Ukraine. — AFP
0ad2b43fe129bb2d: SINGAPORE, Nov 15 — Singapore authorities conducted Exercise Quicksilver 12, a major multi-agency ground deployment exercise, to test operational readiness at the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link’s Woodlands North Station, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said.

More than 600 personnel from the ICA, Singapore Police Force, Singapore Civil Defence Force, Land Transport Authority, Certis CISCO and SMRT Corp participated in the two-day exercise, which began on November 11.

ICA said the exercise aimed to validate operational readiness, response capabilities and inter-agency coordination in managing public security incidents at the station ahead of the operationalisation of the RTS Link.
“The exercise culminated in a coordinated tactical response to resolve a simulated hostage situation at the station.
“The scenario tested the agencies’ ability to coordinate their operational responses, manage evolving threats and bring the incident to a safe resolution,” it said in a Facebook post yesterday.

According to ICA, participating agencies and stakeholders were also tested on their ability to respond to a series of simulated public security incidents, requiring close coordination, timely decision-making and effective deployment of resources.

“ICA will continue to work closely with relevant government agencies and key stakeholders to strengthen inter-agency coordination, enhance operational preparedness and resilience in safeguarding our borders,” it added.
The RTS Link, whcih will connect Bukit Chagar station in Johor Bahru and Woodlands North station in Singapore, is expected to commence operations in February 2027. — Bernama
81166984afd97dd7: KUALA LUMPUR: An SPM student was among 17 individuals detained by the road transport department (JPJ) during a special operation against illegal street racing in the federal capital early this morning.
The student from a secondary school in Petaling Jaya was detained for performing a dangerous "wheelie" stunt.
When approached by reporters, the teenager said he had performed the stunt for fun and claimed he had not realised that JPJ enforcement officers were watching him.
He was detained for investigation under Section 42A(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) for participating in an activity involving speed trials on public roads.
JPJ director-general Aedy Fadly Ramli said the operation covered several locations in Kuala Lumpur, with all those detained brought to Jalan Sultan Ismail for further questioning.

The operation, which began yesterday and ended at about 4.30am today, saw eight individuals investigated under Sections 42A(1) and 42A(2) of Act 333, while another nine were detained for offences involving extreme motorcycle modifications.
“The nine cases are being investigated under several provisions of the Act, depending on the nature of the offences and the level of danger posed,” he told a press conference after the operation.
A total of 1,387 motorcycles were also inspected.
Aedy said the operation was aimed at curbing dangerous driving activities that threatened the safety of other road users.
Since its launch on Oct 25, the special operation under Section 42A has recorded nine cases - six in Kuala Lumpur, two in Selangor and one in Penang.
Section 42A, which came into force on Oct 16, allows enforcement action against illegal racing and speed trials on public roads without waiting for an accident, injury or fatality to occur.
Members of the public can report such activities through the MyJPJ application or by emailing aduantrafik@jpj.gov.my, and may be called upon to assist in investigations.
2b8840c09cbbd8fa: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — A total of 26 candidates forfeited their election deposits after failing to secure at least one-eighth of the total votes counted in the 16th Melaka state election.
Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) recorded the highest number of candidates losing their deposits, with 15 of its 16 candidates failing to secure the minimum number of votes required.
Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) saw five of its seven candidates lose their deposits, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) suffered the same fate with two of its 24 candidates.
Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (Putra), which fielded a sole candidate in the Gadek state seat, and three independent candidates also lost their contests and forfeited their deposits.

Meanwhile, Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Rais Yasin secured the largest winning majority of 16,214 votes in Sungai Udang, defeating the Bersatu and Bersama candidates, who obtained 2,103 and 1,322 votes respectively.
Sungai Udang was among the closely watched seats in the Melaka state election, with 22,195 of its 29,692 registered voters casting their ballots yesterday.

BN candidate Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem, who secured 6,686 votes, recorded the smallest winning majority in a three-cornered contest for the Machap Jaya state seat against PH’s Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin and Bersama’s Prasanth Kumar Brakasam.
Ngwe retained the Machap Jaya seat, which he won with a majority of 938 votes in the 2021 Melaka state election. — Bernama
ad1fbfed9229555f: Sofia Jane has built a screen career spanning more than three decades, taking on roles that demand emotional depth, restraint and an instinctive grasp of human behaviour.
The 54-year-old actress will step into unfamiliar territory with a new challenge: carrying a play entirely on her own, with nothing between her and the audience except for her natural talent.
Her first solo theatrical performance in English, 'Thrown', is far more than just another acting job.
Written by Jodi Gray and directed by Gavin Yap, the production delves into childhood, buried memories and the experiences that shape us long after we think we have left them behind.
At its centre is a child psychologist whose efforts to understand her patients gradually lead her into unsettling territory.
Listening to old audio recordings of her childhood alongside those of her patients, she begins to question where her memories end and someone else's begin.
The premise immediately appealed to Sofia, who sees its themes as particularly timely in a world increasingly aware of mental health and the lasting impact of childhood.

"When I read it, I thought it was very interesting because we are living in a world where mental health challenges affect not just adults but people of all ages, from children to the elderly," she shares.
It is a story that asks uncomfortable questions without offering easy answers. How much of our adult selves is shaped by experiences we barely remember?
Can we trust our memories, especially when they have been revisited, reinterpreted or coloured by the stories of others?
For Sofia, the challenge lies in bringing those questions to life through a single character whose professional understanding of the mind cannot shield her from the doubts of her own past.
ONE ACTRESS, ONE STAGE

Taking on a solo show means there is nowhere to hide. Without fellow actors to share the dramatic weight, Sofia must hold the audience's attention while shifting between the psychologist's professional world and the increasingly blurred landscape of her memories.
"Everything is a challenge," she admits, describing the demands of carrying a performance alone.

Yet the prospect is also a chance to rediscover an art form she has long cherished. Although film and television have defined much of her career, theatre has always held a special pull, waiting for the right role and timing to align.
"Being on stage is something I always look forward to because it has a different energy," she says.
"It feels like starting all over again."
That sense of renewal is fitting for an actress with such an enduring body of work.
Sofia also stresses the importance of choosing material carefully, noting: "A good actor wants a good script. So they will look at who the writer is."

Her decision to take on 'Thrown' reflects that belief. Beyond the demands of a solo piece, the play offers a chance to explore a psychologically complex character and work with Yap for the first time.
For the director, Sofia brings the strength and stage presence needed to anchor the production.
Yap, whose previous stage work includes 'Pewaris', 'Fork It' and 'Eurydice', has often explored themes of memory, grief, inheritance and loss.
He sees the idea of being "thrown" into life as central to the play. Nobody chooses the circumstances of their birth or the environment in which they grow up.
Yet, at certain moments, life pushes us into a new phase and the shift from childhood to adulthood can leave a lasting mark.
THEATRE IN THE AGE OF SCROLLING
Beyond the play itself, Sofia hopes 'Thrown' will remind audiences why theatre is worth experiencing at a time when entertainment is available at the tap of a screen.
For her, the difference is not merely between watching a show at home and seeing one in person. Theatre demands presence.
Audiences must sit together, listen, watch and let a story unfold without the option of scrolling past a difficult moment or hitting pause when their attention wanders.

She believes contemporary theatre continues to evolve through inventive lighting, music and sound, while traditional forms such as Bangsawan, Mak Yong and Indian classical dance remain vital parts of the wider performing arts scene.
Still, keeping the art form alive means facing practical hurdles. Ticket prices can be a barrier and producers need audiences willing to make time for a night out at the theatre.
Sofia believes the exchange between performers and the audience is what makes live performance unique.
A play might stir an uncomfortable memory, spark a fresh perspective or simply leave someone thinking differently about a familiar experience.
"People often linger after a theatre performance," she explains, describing how audiences stay behind to swap thoughts about what they have seen and how it made them feel.
That conversation, she suggests, is part of the experience rather than an afterthought.
Theatre does not end when the house lights come up; its meaning continues to unfold as people talk about what struck a chord with them.
For 'Thrown', an immersive soundscape is designed to pull audiences into the same disorientation felt by the lead character, blurring the line between memory and identity.

Presented by the Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre (JCPAC) and produced by Superbear Productions, 'Thrown' runs at The Studio, JCPAC, in Sunway City from Nov 20 to 22 and Nov 27 to 29, with evening shows at 8.30pm and selected matinees at 3pm.
For Sofia, the invitation is simple: put aside your distractions, sit in the dark and give the story your full attention.
What emerges may be unsettling, moving or unexpectedly familiar — but the experience belongs to the moment, shared between the performer and everyone watching.

79a53290f8b43f9b: PETALING JAYA: A former Umno leader says Barisan Nasional (BN) should dissolve the Pahang and Perak state assemblies next for fresh state elections to be held in both states, where BN still governs with Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Former Batu Pahat MP Puad Zarkashi said BN's cooperation with Perikatan Nasional (PN) was clearly effective, based on the alliance's landslide victory in the Melaka polls yesterday.

Puad added that the pact initially appeared to face obstacles with BN insisting on contesting at least 21 seats, but PAS's decision to give in to BN's demands paid off as the Islamic party still won two challenging seats.
"Therefore, it would only be right for BN to dissolve the Pahang and Perak assemblies next to allow a BN-PN administration to succeed the current unity administrations," he said in a Facebook post.
BN won 21 seats in the Melaka state election yesterday, single-handedly surpassing the two-thirds majority mark, while PN added three more seats to the alliance.
DAP won the remaining four seats for PH.
PN has stated its intention to expand its cooperation with BN nationwide ahead of the next general election, although there has been some resistance in Pahang and Perak.
Two months ago, Pahang menteri besar Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, an Umno vice-president, said BN was capable of retaining the state whether it teams up with PH or PN, or goes solo.
Similarly, a Perak Umno delegate at the party's general assembly had warned that a BN-PN pact could weaken Umno's position in the state.

In the 2022 general election, BN and PN each won 17 state seats in Pahang while PH secured eight. BN subsequently partnered with PH to form the Pahang government, and Wan Rosdy became menteri besar for a second term.

In Perak, BN won only nine state seats in 2022 but Umno's Saarani Mohamad was reappointed as menteri besar after forming the state government with PH, which had secured 24 seats. PN has 26 seats in the Perak state assembly.
a0cd925b9c84ee75: PETALING JAYA: Seorang bekas pemimpin Umno mencadangkan Barisan Nasional (BN) membubarkan Dewan Undangan Negeri (DUN) Pahang dan Perak selepas ini bagi membolehkan PRN baharu diadakan di kedua-dua negeri yang masih ditadbir BN bersama Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Bekas Ahli Parlimen Batu Pahat, Puad Zarkashi, berkata kerjasama BN dengan Perikatan Nasional (PN) terbukti berkesan berdasarkan kemenangan besar gabungan itu dalam PRN Melaka semalam.

Puad berkata, kerjasama itu pada awalnya dilihat berdepan halangan apabila BN bertegas mahu bertanding sekurang-kurangnya 21 kerusi. Namun, keputusan PAS untuk memenuhi tuntutan BN membuahkan hasil apabila parti Islam itu tetap berjaya memenangi dua kerusi yang dianggap sukar.
"Justeru amat wajar DUN Pahang dan Perak bubar untuk menoktahkan kerajaan BN-PN memerintah di dua negeri kerajaan perpaduan itu," katanya di Facebook.
BN memenangi 21 kerusi dalam PRN Melaka semalam, sekali gus memperoleh majoriti dua pertiga dengan kekuatan sendiri, manakala PN menambah tiga lagi kerusi kepada gabungan itu.
DAP pula memenangi baki empat kerusi untuk PH.
PN sebelum ini menyatakan hasrat untuk memperluas kerjasamanya dengan BN di seluruh negara menjelang PRU akan datang, meskipun terdapat tentangan di Pahang dan Perak.

Dua bulan lalu, Menteri Besar Pahang Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, yang juga naib presiden Umno, berkata BN mampu mempertahankan negeri itu sama ada bekerjasama dengan PH atau PN, mahupun bertanding secara solo.
Seorang perwakilan Umno Perak pada perhimpunan agung parti itu sebelum ini juga memberi amaran bahawa kerjasama BN-PN boleh melemahkan kedudukan Umno di negeri berkenaan.

Dalam PRU 2022, BN dan PN masing-masing memenangi 17 kerusi DUN di Pahang, manakala PH memperoleh lapan kerusi. BN kemudiannya bekerjasama dengan PH untuk membentuk kerajaan negeri Pahang, dengan Wan Rosdy dilantik semula sebagai menteri besar bagi penggal kedua.

Di Perak, BN hanya memenangi sembilan kerusi DUN pada 2022, namun pemimpin Umno Saarani Mohamad dilantik semula sebagai menteri besar selepas membentuk kerajaan negeri bersama PH, yang memenangi 24 kerusi. PN pula mempunyai 26 kerusi dalam DUN Perak.
6c6f7f87396c9867: NEW YORK: Electric vehicle growth has hit a speed bump in the United States, but hybrid autos are gaining market share thanks to the jump in fuel prices due to the Iran war.

Rising popularity of hybrids – which can run on either gasoline or an electric charge – has been a source of US sales increases for Japanese and South Korean carmakers in 2026, prompting fresh investments from both established and new players in that segment of the market.
Honda, a long-time rival to US hybrid market leader Toyota, announced this week $3 billion to build a new hybrid plant in Ohio and add capacity at plants in two other states.

Nissan, which is launching its first significant hybrid product for the US market this fall, realized its absence in the category was denting sales, said Ponz Pandikuthira, a senior vice president at Nissan Americas.
"We were losing that traffic," Pandikuthira said, adding that many customers want to at least explore and test drive a hybrid even if they end up buying an internal-combustion engine (ICE) vehicle.

General Motors, which avoided the category earlier in the 2020s when it invested heavily in electric vehicles, plans hybrids "in multiple segments, the key segments that we participate in," Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mary Barra said last month on a conference call.
"We'll talk more about them as we get closer to the launch," Barra said in response to a question from a Wall Street analyst on an earnings call.

Hybrid electric vehicle volumes have risen by more than a fifth since the middle of 2025, resulting in market share of 16.3 per cent at the end of the second quarter, according to Cox Automotive, an auto services and technology provider.

That's a record and up from 13 per cent a year earlier. The increase stood in contrast with declines in the share of ICE and EV vehicles, with the latter suffering from the elimination of US tax credits under legislation signed by US President Donald Trump.
Gasoline prices have been above $4 a gallon for much of 2026 due to the Middle East war. Prices currently average $3.87 per gallon, according to the American Automobile Association.
MORE OPTIONS
Nissan's US campaign in the category will begin with the Rogue, a hybrid version of the compact SUV that has been the Japanese automaker's top-selling ICE product in the United States.
Nissan has introduced two generations of hybrid vehicles in other markets but began working a few years ago on a version better suited to US driving conditions.
"When we use the system in Japan and in Europe, they're mostly in urban driving conditions, which just shines because you're doing stop-and-go traffic," Pandikuthira said.
The new Rogue being unveiled is "optimised for US driving conditions, so that's why it's a home run with climbing, with lots of use on the highway," Pandikuthira said.

The vehicle's other selling point is Nissan's vehicle architecture, in which the electric powertrain exclusively drives the wheels, meaning the gasoline-powered engine is only a source of neutrons but doesn't actually propel the vehicle.
That system, which Nissan markets as "e-POWER", is designed for a quieter, smoother ride than other hybrid models that drive on a gasoline-fuelled engine.

In going with the Rogue, Nissan is picking the most popular vehicle segment for hybrids in the US market. Led by the Toyota RAV-4 and the Honda-CRV, compact SUVs account for about 30 per cent of US hybrid sales, said Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox.

Valdez Streaty attributes the growth in hybrids not only to higher gasoline prices but also to greater vehicle choice on the market following product introductions from more recent hybrid entrants, including South Korean brands Kia and Hyundai.
She predicted that additional hybrids in popular vehicle classes like pickup trucks or full-sized SUVs could sell well.
"It definitely has room to grow," Valdez Streaty said of the hybrid's market share.

37080af6409563bb: BAGHDAD: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine officials on Saturday, following an investigation into allegations of oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hizbollah group.
Baghdad faces mounting US pressure to rein in Teheran-backed armed groups and curb Iran's influence, a difficult task in a country long caught between its two key allies, the US and Iran.

Zaidi, who came to power with US blessing, had launched earlier this week a probe into oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area – a stronghold of Kataeb Hizbollah, which Washington designates a terrorist organisation – in Babylon province, south of Baghdad.

"In light of the investigation's findings," Zaidi "ordered that all individuals accused of involvement in oil smuggling operations be referred to the judiciary," his military spokesman Sabah al-Numan said, without identifying the suspects.

The premier "also ordered the dismissal" of nine officials, including security and intelligence officers in Babylon province, an interior ministry commander, and the director of the Oil Pipelines Company at the oil ministry.
Numan did not elaborate on the role of the sacked officials in the alleged smuggling operations.
A committee investigating the allegations entered Jurf al-Sakher on Friday, accompanied by members of Kataeb Hizbollah.

On Wednesday, the state news agency INA reported that "intelligence documents" containing satellite images "showed crude oil and oil-derivatives smuggling operations carried out by an armed faction" in Jurf al-Sakher, accusing the unnamed faction of tapping into a pipeline there.
According to Numan, the investigating committee "confirmed the accuracy" of the information.

Tensions have mounted between Zaidi and Kataeb Hizbollah since the prime minister, who enjoys close relations with the US, vowed to ensure that armed factions would hand over their weapons to the state.
While some groups said they would disarm, other powerful factions, mainly Kataeb Hizbollah, refused to do so.
Senior Iraqi politicians previously told AFP that Zaidi had repeatedly said he was ready to "confront" groups if they do not disarm.
Kataeb Hizbollah has recently issued several sharp statements against the prime minister, accusing him of corruption and threatening his government.
A senior Iraqi politician told AFP that "it has become personal" between Zaidi and Kataeb Hizbollah, adding that political leaders were working to defuse tensions.

Washington has accused Iraqi armed groups of involvement in oil smuggling. It has also sanctioned Iraqi officials and entities for blending Iraqi and Iranian oil or selling Iranian oil as Iraqi to help Tehran evade sanctions.

d1cc457afa6c36df: STARBASE: SpaceX has caught the upper stage of its giant Starship rocket system for the first time after it returned to Earth on Saturday after a test flight into space, German Press Agency (dpa) reported.

About 20 hours after launch, the Starship returned to the Starbase spaceport in southern Texas, where mechanical arms on the launch tower caught it. It was the first time SpaceX had attempted such a catch.
The test flight had earlier suffered a setback, when its lower stage splashed down in the sea and burst into flames instead of being caught by the launch tower as planned.

The company, owned by tech billionaire Elon Musk, initially gave no information about the possible cause of the failure. The lower stage, known as the Super Heavy booster, had been successfully caught during three previous test flights.

The upper stage, also called Starship, entered Earth's orbit shortly after separating from the booster and deployed satellites for SpaceX's internet service Starlink. It then orbited the Earth several times.
Starship's last test flight took place in September when the rocket reached Earth's orbit for the first time, before make a controlled splashdown in the Pacific Ocean about three hours later.
Standing around 120 metres tall, Starship is the largest rocket system ever built, with both stages designed to be reusable.
The system was first tested in April 2023, when it exploded completely after a few minutes. Subsequent tests have had mixed success.
NASA plans to use Starship to send astronauts to the moon, while SpaceX hopes eventually to reach Mars.
c677a2bbe3db074a: MADRID: England's manager Thomas Tuchel does not expect racist abuse during Sunday's Nations League clash with Spain but said his players would be reminded of anti-racism protocols, prompting a terse response from Spain's coach Luis de la Fuente.

England face the world champions in Madrid with top spot in their Nations League group at stake, returning to the Spanish capital for the first time since a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were subjected to racist abuse from the crowd.
England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.

"In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed," Rice told reporters on Saturday. "We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"I'm not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one."
The issue gained traction after Spain were fined $20,000 following anti-Muslim chants by supporters during a match against Egypt in Barcelona in March.
Spain must also play their next home friendly with a reduced-capacity crowd as part of the punishment.
Meanwhile, De la Fuente rejected any suggestion that racism was a problem in Spain.
"What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it," De la Fuente said.
"There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist."
Tuchel bristled when told of De la Fuente's remarks, accusing sections of the Spanish media of misrepresenting his comments.
"I was polite enough to (answer) a question from your colleagues, and you run and ask the other coach and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain," Tuchel said.
"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth."
James Trafford will start in goal for England on Saturday, said Tuchel, who added that everyone was fit to play including Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence who have recovered from injury.

067602789db2ad54: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The day finally arrived for Malaysian singer Aina Abdul to take the stage at the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, performing her track Bluest Sky.

Performing as the 11th and final contestant, she finished fourth in the competition yesterday in Bangkok, Thailand, scoring 152 points, which comprised 82 points from the professional jury and 70 from the public vote.
The Philippines’ Carmelle emerged as the competition’s first champion with 211 points, followed by Thailand’s Mang x Daou with 170 points and Vietnam’s Tóc Tiên with 164 points.
Beyond bringing Bluest Sky to an international audience, Aina complemented her performance with a distinctive stage presentation that told a story through visual symbolism.
Her performance featured a concept centred on water, using the element to represent sadness and emotions often kept inside.

The performance began with visuals of a single drop of water before gradually building into a massive wave, reflecting the growing intensity of emotions and the difficulty of letting go of a deep love.
The concept was further brought to life through a giant water-drop-shaped stage prop, LED visuals and a costume by Malaysian fashion designer Melinda Looi.
Featuring turquoise blue and translucent details, the outfit complemented the water theme that ran throughout the performance.
At the end of her performance, Aina greeted the audience with, “Assalamualaikum Thailand, may you find your Bluest Sky in your life.”
“Khop khun khap (Thank you),” she added.
Despite finishing outside the top three, Aina received an outpouring of support from Malaysians, with many taking to TV3’s Instagram page to congratulate her on the performance.
“You did your best, Aina.
“Thank you for your performance!”” one commenter wrote.
Another said: “It’s okay, Aina! You’ve already won the hearts of Malaysians!”
Other comments included: “Congratulations Aina Abdul and “It’s not easy to achieve this level of success.
“Never tire of continuing to make the country proud!”

Aina’s appearance at the international competition marks another milestone in her career, following her success at the 40th Anugerah Juara Lagu (AJL40), where she won Best Performance for Kamu and the Shopee Choice Artist Icon award.
She was subsequently selected to represent Malaysia at Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026.
The competition marked the first Asian edition of the long-running Eurovision Song Contest, bringing together performers from across the region to compete with original songs.

Organised by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), Voxovation and S2O Productions, the competition adopted a 50:50 voting system, with equal contributions from professional juries and the public vote.
Aina wrote Bluest Sky as an English-language power ballad about love, heartbreak, and uncertainty, with a message of hope that even the deepest sadness will eventually pass.
The song features a musical arrangement by Mac Chew, with multiple instrumental layers contributing to its sweeping sound.
