e676acede33d79c4: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — French President Emmanuel Macron will undertake an official visit to Malaysia on Nov 16 and 17, marking his first trip to the country.

The Malaysia visit will follow Macron’s state visit to Cambodia from Nov 14 to 16, where he is expected to focus on strengthening bilateral relations, particularly in economic affairs, culture and healthcare.

The visit is expected to usher in a new chapter in Malaysia-France relations, with both countries set to elevate their longstanding ties to a strategic partnership covering defence and security, critical minerals, the energy transition, aeronautics and space, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and semiconductors.

According to the French Presidency, the two countries will develop their cooperation based on common priorities, while strengthening collaboration on major regional and international issues, as well as relations between Europe and Asean.

France described Malaysia as a key partner of France and the European Union (EU) within Asean, highlighting Malaysia’s chairmanship of the regional bloc in 2025 and the two countries’ shared commitment to multilateralism and compliance with international law.

“France and Malaysia are both committed to multilateralism and compliance with international law, and are working to support peace and stability in Southeast Asia and in the Indo-Pacific,” the Presidency said, noting France’s distinctive role in the region through its overseas territories.
The French Presidency provided the information in a background briefing ahead of the visit, which the French Embassy in Malaysia shared with Bernama on Friday.
The visit builds on the momentum generated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s official visit to France in July 2025, the first by a Malaysian head of government in 15 years.
The French Presidency described Macron’s upcoming visit as “a new step” in bilateral relations.

On economic relations, the Presidency said France was Malaysia’s 10th-largest economic partner and ranked third among the EU’s member states, with bilateral trade reaching €4.7 billion (approximately RM21.23 billion) in 2025, an increase of 11 per cent from 2024.

“There is a significant French economic presence, with around 300 subsidiaries of French companies and 300 French-owned businesses under local law, employing some 30,000 people,” it said, adding that France was Malaysia’s 12th-largest investor and second-largest European investor in 2025.

On critical minerals, the Presidency said cooperation between the two countries was taking a step forward, driven by a shared ambition to diversify and secure strategic supplies by strengthening their respective ecosystems across the entire value chain.
It cited the industrial partnership between French company Carester and Malaysian firm Malaco Mining, signed in 2025 during Anwar’s visit to Paris.
The partnership aims to develop local rare earth element mining and separation capabilities while meeting the highest environmental and social standards.

In the energy and technology sectors, France said cooperation included the energy transition, civil nuclear energy, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon capture projects, while highlighting the complementary strengths of both countries in semiconductors.

“Complementarity between Malaysian capacities in the manufacture and packaging of semiconductors and French expertise in research, design and specialised technologies opens up cooperation possibilities that will help diversify and strengthen the resilience of global supply chains in this key sector,” it said.
The last visit by a French President to Malaysia was in March 2017, when then-President Francois Hollande undertook a two-day state visit to the country.
The visit marked an important milestone in Malaysia-France bilateral relations, coinciding with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries
Meanwhile, Macron’s Nov 14-16 visit to Cambodia will focus on renewing and deepening bilateral relations, particularly in economic affairs, culture and healthcare.

He will also attend the 20th Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh on Nov 15 and 16, bringing together representatives of 90 states and governments under the theme “Reinvest in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Sustainable Stability”.

The Cambodian visit will also focus on strengthening cooperation in infrastructure, energy, healthcare, transport, agriculture and heritage preservation, while reaffirming the longstanding relationship between the two countries, which dates back to the 1991 Paris Peace Agreements. — Bernama
02566e4756157aa7: LETTER:By 2030, Malaysia will have entered the ranks of ageing societies, with nearly five million people aged 60 and above.
This is a demographic milestone and a profound transformation of how we live, work, care and organise our economies.
Our response remains largely defensive. Ageing is discussed principally in terms of pension liabilities, healthcare expenditure, dependency ratios and the financial burden on families.
But framing ageing exclusively as a welfare problem obscures an opportunity of extraordinary economic and social significance.
The emerging silver economy - the goods, services, technologies and infrastructure serving older people - is becoming one of the world's most consequential economic frontiers.
China offers a striking illustration. It sees its silver economy as a new growth driver estimated at around seven trillion yuan (approximately US$1 trillion) in 2024.
Projections suggest it could reach RMB30 trillion by 2035, equivalent to around 10 per cent of China's GDP.

What is emerging is not simply a market for nursing homes and medical services, but an ecosystem encompassing assistive technologies, robotics, smart homes, accessible transport, financial services, lifelong learning and new forms of employment.
We need to rethink ageing itself. Malaysia has considerable advantages.
It possesses an established healthcare sector, a multilingual population, relatively competitive operating costs and growing digital infrastructure.
Its location within Asean offers access to a regional market whose demographic transition is already underway.
Yet Malaysia has barely begun to articulate what a national silver economy might look like.

We lack a comprehensive assessment of its market potential, an integrated strategy for developing ageing-related industries, and a framework connecting innovation, investment, care provision and employment.
Retirement security remains precarious for many. Families struggle to reconcile employment with caregiving. Informal care facilities operate in regulatory grey zones.
Older people encounter neighbourhoods, transport systems and public spaces that are often inaccessible or hostile to their needs.
These are not simply social-sector problems. They represent unmet demand, lost economic opportunities and failures of public policy.
Artificial intelligence could fundamentally change the economics of ageing.
China's pursuit of AI and robotics is driven by multiple strategic considerations, including technological competition and industrial productivity.
But its demographic transition adds another important dimension.
As the population ages and the workforce contracts, automation becomes increasingly important not merely for economic competitiveness, but for sustaining productivity and care.
AI-enabled technologies can support fall detection, medication management, remote monitoring, predictive healthcare and assistive robotics.
They can help older people remain independent for longer, while enabling caregivers and healthcare professionals to work more effectively.
Crucially, technology should extend human care, not replace it. Ageing is also about loneliness, dignity, belonging and human relationships.
Malaysia's investments in AI infrastructure present an opportunity we should not squander.
Beyond hosting data centres, we could develop regional capabilities in multilingual eldercare technologies, intelligent home systems, digital health services and AI-assisted care management.
Our universities, technology companies and healthcare institutions could collaborate to develop solutions relevant not only to Malaysia, but to the wider Global South.
Consider the popular proposition of ageing in place - allowing older people to remain in their homes and communities rather than institutional care. It is an attractive principle.
But what does it mean in a neighbourhood with broken pavements, inaccessible public transport, unsafe public spaces, poorly maintained lifts and weak community support?
The silver economy cannot flourish in a society where the public systems necessary for its development remain dysfunctional. Malaysia still has time to act.

But the window is narrowing. We need a national silver economy strategy that connects industrial policy with social policy; mobilises private investment while professionalising care; harnesses AI while protecting dignity; and develops age-friendly communities as productive, inclusive places rather than merely spaces for managing dependency.
The silver wave is coming. Ageing will test the quality of our institutions and also reveal the limits of our imagination. The question is whether Malaysia will merely grow old or grow wiser.
DR SHAHRIDAN FAIEZ
Think City, Kuala Lumpur

14b54b5510f51af3: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian women-led social enterprise Kloth Circularity has emerged as one of three winners of the 2026 APEC Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) Award, in recognition of its efforts to transform discarded textiles into economic opportunities while empowering underserved communities.

According to a statement issued by the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Secretariat, the enterprise collects unwanted textiles and repurposes them into new products, while providing sewing and upcycling training to women from underserved communities to help them develop skills and generate income.

Kloth Circularity was recognised alongside two other small businesses from Hong Kong, China and Indonesia for their innovative approaches to converting food, agricultural and textile waste into economic opportunities while supporting local communities.
The winners were announced at the Concluding Senior Officials' Meeting in Shenzhen on Saturday.

Kloth Circularity co-founder Sarah Kedah said the enterprise hoped its journey would demonstrate how circularity could create livelihoods, strengthen local value chains and generate economic opportunities.
"It cannot be achieved by one organisation alone, which is why we bring together businesses, communities and policymakers to make it work," she said.

Meanwhile, Hong Kong-based Feeding Hong Kong, founded by Gabrielle Kirstein, was recognised for its work in collecting surplus food stocks from businesses and redistributing them through charities to people in need.
Since its establishment in 2011, the organisation has rescued more than 10,000 tonnes of food, helping to provide 32 million meals.

Indonesia's Plana, meanwhile, was recognised for transforming rice husks and plastic waste into durable alternatives to natural timber for furniture and construction, helping to reduce pressure on forests.

Its co-founder Joshua Christopher Chandra said the initiative also provided additional income opportunities for farmers and waste collectors through the purchase of agricultural byproducts and plastic waste.
The APEC BCG Award recognises micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) whose business models support the Bangkok Goals on Bio-Circular-Green Economy, adopted by APEC Economic Leaders in 2022.

APEC Secretariat executive director Eduardo Pedrosa said MSMEs accounted for more than 97 per cent of businesses across the region, making their role in sustainable economic development particularly significant.
"APEC's role is to help their ideas reach more markets and more communities," he added.

bcb6bfcb1e875f3a: SINGAPORE, Nov 15 — Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto netted his first international goal with a late winner as Japan edged Brazil 3-2 in a thrilling friendly at the National Stadium in Singapore yesterday.
A brilliant brace by Vinicius Junior had erased a two-goal deficit after strikes by Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the Samurai Blue 2-0 up in the opening 19 minutes.
But Sakamoto was in the right place to fire home after latching on to Kodai Sano’s deflected effort in stoppage time to give the Asian side a dramatic victory in front of 38,688 fans.
In the first meeting between the teams since Brazil’s 2-1 win in the round of 32 at the World Cup last June, the Samurai Blue seized the early initiative with two goals in a torrid four-minute spell.
On 15 minutes, a through ball by Ritsu Doan was picked up just inside the Brazilian half by Kubo who showed quick feet to cut inside Jair before firing a low effort past goalkeeper Pedro Morisco.

Japan added another shortly afterwards after some fine work by Shuto Nakano, who broke down the right flank and centred for an unmarked Nakamura to calmly place a right-footed shot into the bottom corner of the net.
Brazil responded with a magnificent goal by Vinicius in the 33rd minute.

Zion Suzuki had made an excellent stop to deny Estevao when he bore down on goal, but the Japan goalkeeper could do little when the ball fell to Vinicius who found the top corner with a right-footed diagonal drive.
Suzuki made good stops to deny Brazilian debutant Andre just before half-time and skipper Raphinha after the interval as Japan clung to their narrow lead.

But the Selecao were not to be denied and Vinicius put them back on level terms in the 75th minute with another fine finish as he cut in from the left flank and launched a low right-footed effort that found the net off the right post.
Brazil went close to grabbing the winner as substitute Endrick rocked the crossbar with a fierce effort and Joao Gomes sent a low shot narrowly wide.
But in stoppage time, an effort by Kodai Sano took a fortunate bounce off a defender and fell nicely for Sakamoto to send the ball past Pedro Morisco.
Brazil appealed for a foul in the build-up to the goal but VAR upheld the goal and Raphinha was shown a red card for his vehement protests. — AFP
2badc2f099d3e9e9: MADRID, Nov 15 — The 2030 World Cup final will be in Spain, Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) head Rafael Louzan reiterated yesterday, adding that he is not considering “withdrawing” should he be wrong.
Spain is organising the next World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. The decision on the venue for the final will be made in 2028, Louzan said.

Spain favours Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium for the final. Portugal does not have a suitable stadium but Morocco has suggested the 115,000-capacity Hassan II Stadium being built in Benslimane near Casablanca.
“There is no other plan than for the final to be held in Spain,” said Louzan at a conference at the RFEF’s Ciudad del Futbol on the outskirts of Madrid.
“I am not currently considering the possibility of withdrawing from Spain, as the prospect of Spain not hosting the final is not on the table,” he said.
Louzan was responding to Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the right-wing People’s Party.

In a television interview on November 5, Feijoo said that were he to become prime minister in the general election on November 29, he would advocate withdrawing Spain’s bid to host the World Cup should Morocco be awarded the final.
Luzon said the question was entirely hypothetical.
“That notion simply doesn’t exist,” he said, adding that under Fifa’s tradition of rotating the World Cup the staging of the final “belongs to the European continent”.
A delegation of Fifa technical experts spent last week visiting Spanish stadiums that are hoping to host matches during the tournament, Louzan said. — AFP
dced7b6925d7aa4d: MANILA: Asean foreign ministers are seeking to fast-track the establishment of a regional coordination centre for transboundary haze control, the Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported.

The renewed call was made during the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Pasay City on Saturday amid growing concerns over severe haze pollution that recently affected several Southeast Asian countries.
Widespread forest fires in Indonesia have triggered severe haze, with thick smog drifting as far as the Philippines and prompting class cancellations in the second half of the year.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said Indonesia, in the meeting, conveyed that it is acting on the issue and exerting its best to address the haze pollution.
Singapore and Malaysia, she added, were "very cordial" to the statement made by Indonesia.

"Singapore remarked positively, and Malaysia, the same thing. So, I think that there had been discussions, and perhaps the actions taken by Indonesia was really very sweeping and really helped what is happening," she said.
She said discussions on haze covered ongoing national actions and regional cooperation specifically aimed at mitigating land and forest fires.
The regional bloc adopted the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2002 to prevent and monitor transboundary haze pollution caused by land or forest fires.
Under the deal, the bloc is mandated to put up the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC) to manage the impact of said pollution. — BERNAMA
b7e95e0cecdfee07: PETALING JAYA: “Everybody has desires. It is simply part of being human,” said Tay Eng Chye, rather matter-of-factly.

For an artist whose paintings have long celebrated the tenderness of family life, friendship and human connection, this might seem an unexpected admission. But the 79-year-old is not particularly interested in drawing distinctions between the subjects artists are expected to explore and those they are not.

His latest exhibition, "Unseen / Ob:seen" at AweGallery here, offers a glimpse into this less familiar side of his artistic practice, bringing together more than 30 paintings and etchings from his private archives, some of which have remained unseen for decades.
Among them is a collection of works exploring physical intimacy and desire, subjects that Tay has largely kept away from public view.
"We don't necessarily show that side of ourselves, but it’s part of life," he said. "Sometimes, these thoughts and experiences find their way into my paintings."
The decision to exhibit them was not driven by a sudden desire to provoke or challenge convention. Some were made purely for his own enjoyment, with no intention of ever displaying them.
"I think it is time to share some of these works that I have kept to myself for so long," he mentioned.

Nor is he particularly concerned about how audiences might receive them. "As an artist, you should put your work out there. Everyone has different opinions, and I don't expect everyone to like everything I create. That's perfectly normal."

It is an attitude that perhaps reflects the independence with which Tay has approached his career. Born in Bukit Besar, Kedah, in 1947, he grew up in a small, isolated settlement where life was a far cry from the artistic circles he would eventually inhabit in New York.

His childhood was modest, and he recalls a household where family members rarely spoke to one another. “My mom had passed away, and my dad was always busy with work. I was by myself most of the time,” he recalled.
He was not particularly successful at school either, struggling especially with English. Art, however, offered an alternative.

In 1968, aged 20, he moved to New York to study at the Art Students League, graduating from the School of Visual Arts in 1972 with a qualification in graphic design. He subsequently worked in the design industry while developing his own artistic practice on the side.
"I was lucky, but opportunities alone are not enough. You have to work hard. If you don't put in the effort, nothing is going to happen," he said.

He gradually built a following through limited-edition prints, eventually reaching international collectors. In 1993, he established his New York studio, Tapir Editions, while continuing to develop a distinctive style centred on everyday moments of family, music and human connection, expressed through distinctive figures with rounded faces and simplified features.
"I'm not interested in painting realistically. My subjects are meant to be universal; they could be anybody, anywhere in the world," he explained.

Some of his paintings also carry unexpected personal connections. One painting in the exhibition was inspired by a 1996 visit to France's Lascaux caves, where he saw prehistoric animal paintings while accompanying his late wife, an American archaeology professor, on a research trip.
Such encounters, he said, do not always translate immediately into artwork. “Sometimes an experience simply stays with me until I find a way to express it. It can take several years.”

That willingness to experiment continues to define his practice. Looking at some of the older paintings, he commented: “I wonder if I might have chosen different colours or approached a composition differently. But this is part of an artist's natural progression. We are always growing.”

Perhaps that is what makes "Unseen / Ob:seen" particularly revealing. Beyond the erotic works, the exhibition offers a glimpse of an artist who has never confined himself to the subjects audiences associate with his name.
"I simply want to try something different. I don't necessarily know where it will lead," Tay concluded.
'Unseen / Ob:seen' (until Nov 23)

2dd1bd3885f277c2: MELAKA: Bersama must rethink its approach to identity politics if it hopes to avoid political irrelevance, says an analyst following the party’s second electoral wipeout this year in the Melaka state election yesterday.

Ahmad Fauzi Abdul Hamid of Universiti Sains Malaysia said Bersama’s political ideology was out of step with the country’s identity-based politics, which had shaped electoral behaviour since Malaysia’s independence.
“Communal identity still dominates the ballot. Identity politics is a constant; it won’t disappear unless we reach a new national consensus that calls for new constitutional arrangements.
“Bersama is living in its own bubble, one free from racial politics, which is too idealistic, at least for the present time,” he told FMT.
As an example, he cited Bersama’s performance in Gadek, where it was beaten by more than 1,000 votes by Putra, a party he described as championing ultra-nationalism.

BN’s S Nadarajah, who secured 6,472 votes, won the seat with a 3,514-vote majority over PH's Jegasilan K. Putra’s Laila Norinda Maon claimed 1,317 votes, while Bersama's B Laveen garnered only 287 votes.
Fauzi said Putra’s nationalist approach appeared to resonate more with voters than Bersama’s liberal platform.
He also said Bersama was in an awkward position because as a splinter party from PKR, it lacked the influence to attract Pakatan Harapan (PH) voters despite their broadly liberal outlook.
“Liberals of all races couldn’t afford to ‘waste’ their votes on Bersama since PH is already embattled in its present condition.
“Unless there are special reasons backing a particular Bersama candidate, a rational PH voter would not risk voting for them,” he said.

Fauzi said Bersama needed to incorporate identity politics into its electoral strategy if it hoped to make any meaningful progress, including in its plans to contest up to 20 parliamentary seats in the next general election.
“Malaysia’s political system wasn’t designed as a liberal democratic order that some political idealists pretend it to be. Identity politics is a baseline,” he said.
Bersama still building

Although Bersama failed to win any seats in Melaka, some of its candidates managed to retain their deposits. In Bemban, its candidate Dr Solehin Saleh secured 4,140 votes, finishing second behind incumbent Perikatan Nasional candidate Dr Yadzil Yaakub, who won the seat with 11,881 votes.
Solehin secured 22.5% of the votes, comfortably above the 12.5% threshold required to retain his deposit.
This marked an improvement from Bersama’s performance in the Johor state election, where all 15 of its candidates lost their deposits.
Prior to yesterday’s polls, Wong Chen, one of Bersama’s key leaders, said the party had aimed to increase its vote share to 12% in Melaka, from 6% in Johor.
Asrul Sani of political consultancy The Asia Group agreed that the party’s progress should be measured by its share of the vote rather than the number of seats won.
“Bersama is still building its party machinery, so its performance should be assessed by its share of the vote across the seats it contested and whether it is establishing an electoral base.
"Not winning a seat at this stage is not necessarily a setback,” he told FMT.
However, Asrul questioned how long Bersama could rely on vote share as a measure of progress without translating that support into electoral victories.
“A strong vote share would give it a foundation to keep building, but it will eventually need a credible path to winning seats,” he said.
cad99f84ed47fd5a: MELAKA: Bersama perlu memikirkan semula pendekatannya terhadap politik identiti jika mahu mengelak daripada menjadi tidak relevan dalam arena politik, kata seorang penganalisis susulan kekalahan besar kedua parti itu dalam pilihan raya tahun ini pada PRN Melaka semalam.

Ahmad Fauzi Abdul Hamid dari Universiti Sains Malaysia berkata, ideologi politik Bersama tidak seiring dengan politik berteraskan identiti di negara ini, yang telah membentuk tingkah laku pengundi sejak Malaysia mencapai kemerdekaan.

“Identiti komunal masih mendominasi peti undi. Politik identiti merupakan sesuatu yang berterusan dan tidak akan hilang melainkan kita mencapai konsensus nasional baharu yang menuntut aturan perlembagaan baharu.
“Bersama hidup dalam gelembungnya sendiri, yang bebas daripada politik perkauman. Pendekatan itu terlalu idealistik, sekurang-kurangnya buat masa ini,” katanya kepada FMT.

Sebagai contoh, beliau merujuk kepada prestasi Bersama di Gadek, apabila parti itu tewas dengan majoriti lebih 1,000 undi kepada Putra, sebuah parti yang disifatkannya sebagai memperjuangkan fahaman nasionalisme melampau.

Calon BN S Nadarajah, yang memperoleh 6,472 undi, memenangi kerusi itu dengan majoriti 3,514 undi mengatasi calon PH Jegasilan K. Laila Norinda Maon daripada Putra pula memperoleh 1,317 undi, manakala calon Bersama B Laveen, hanya meraih 287 undi.
Fauzi berkata, pendekatan nasionalisme Putra dilihat lebih mendapat sambutan pengundi berbanding platform liberal Bersama.

Beliau turut berkata, Bersama berada dalam kedudukan yang serba sukar kerana sebagai parti serpihan PKR, parti itu tidak mempunyai pengaruh untuk menarik pengundi Pakatan Harapan (PH), meskipun mereka secara umumnya mempunyai kecenderungan liberal.
“Golongan liberal daripada semua kaum tidak sanggup ‘membazirkan’ undi mereka kepada Bersama memandangkan PH sendiri sedang berdepan pelbagai cabaran dalam keadaan sekarang.
“Melainkan terdapat sebab-sebab khusus yang menyokong seseorang calon Bersama, pengundi PH yang rasional tidak akan mengambil risiko mengundi mereka,” katanya.

Fauzi berkata, Bersama perlu memasukkan elemen politik identiti dalam strategi pilihan rayanya jika mahu mencapai sebarang kemajuan bermakna, termasuk dalam perancangannya untuk bertanding sehingga 20 kerusi Parlimen pada PRU akan datang.
“Sistem politik Malaysia tidak dibentuk sebagai sebuah sistem demokrasi liberal seperti yang digambarkan oleh sesetengah golongan idealis politik. Politik identiti ialah asasnya,” katanya.
Bersama masih membina kekuatan

Walaupun gagal memenangi sebarang kerusi di Melaka, beberapa calon Bersama berjaya memperoleh undi yang mencukupi untuk mengekalkan wang deposit mereka. Di Bemban, calonnya Dr Solehin Saleh memperoleh 4,140 undi, menduduki tempat kedua di belakang penyandang daripada Perikatan Nasional (PN) Dr Yadzil Yaakub, yang memenangi kerusi itu dengan 11,881 undi.
Solehin memperoleh 22.5% undi, jauh melepasi ambang 12.5% yang diperlukan untuk mengekalkan wang deposit.
Prestasi itu menunjukkan peningkatan berbanding pencapaian Bersama dalam PRN Johor, apabila kesemua 15 calonnya kehilangan wang deposit.
Sebelum PRN Melaka semalam, Wong Chen, antara pemimpin utama Bersama, berkata parti itu menyasarkan peningkatan peratusan undinya kepada 12% di Melaka, berbanding 6% di Johor.
Asrul Sani daripada firma perunding politik The Asia Group bersetuju bahawa kemajuan parti itu wajar diukur berdasarkan peratusan undi yang diperoleh, bukannya jumlah kerusi yang dimenangi.

“Bersama masih membina jentera partinya, justeru prestasinya perlu dinilai berdasarkan peratusan undi yang diperoleh di semua kerusi yang ditandinginya serta sama ada parti itu berjaya membina asas sokongan pengundi.
“Tidak memenangi sebarang kerusi pada peringkat ini tidak semestinya satu kemunduran,” katanya kepada FMT.
Bagaimanapun, Asrul mempersoalkan berapa lama Bersama boleh terus menggunakan peratusan undi sebagai ukuran kemajuan tanpa menterjemahkan sokongan itu kepada kemenangan pilihan raya.
“Peratusan undi yang tinggi akan memberikannya asas untuk terus berkembang, tetapi akhirnya parti itu perlu mempunyai laluan yang meyakinkan untuk memenangi kerusi,” katanya.
e3f41626fec62c9e: NOVEMBER 15 — Malaysia is fast entering a demographic transition that will fundamentally transform its social and economic landscape.
The latest figures from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) show that citizens aged 65 years and above now make up 8.4 per cent of the total population.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

For many seniors living outside the main districts, the closest PAWE is tens of kilometres away, essentially creating huge geographic deserts where the most vulnerable segments of the population are excluded from community support. — Pexels pic

The country’s median age is 31.7 years old and its old-age dependency ratio is 11.9, putting it on a path to becoming a full “aged nation” – when 14 per cent of the population is aged 65 or older – by 2040.

In response to these changes in demographic profile, the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) through the 2011 National Policy for Older Persons (Dasar Warga Emas Negara, DWEN) has incorporated active ageing and community integration as a key component of national social policy.
But those macroeconomic numbers hide a rising human dilemma: widespread social isolation among the elderly.

While policy frameworks emphasise the importance of daily social interaction, lifelong learning, and active health monitoring to prevent cognitive and physical decline in seniors, the practical implementation of these measures is severely limited by spatial inequities, the physical distance between locations, and ongoing deficiencies in public transportation throughout the country.

The Pusat Aktiviti Warga Emas (PAWE) is the heart of the community-based active ageing strategy in Malaysia, a welfare facility initiative under the management of the Department of Social Welfare (Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat, JKM) in strategic collaboration with the local district councils and non-governmental organisations.

Across the country, some 217 PAWE centres are functioning to provide day activity hubs for mobile citizens aged 60 and above to avail health check-ups, physical exercise, religious studies and online literacy workshops.
Researchers and urban planners emphasise the necessity of these centres for social inclusion, but there is a substantial spatial mismatch in their physical distribution.
Most PAWE facilities are found in the high-density urban clusters, state capitals and major district centers in Penang, Perak and the Klang Valley (Kuala Lumpur and Selangor).
In contrast, in suburban peripheral areas, agricultural settlements and rural kampungs are suffering from acute spatial scarcity.

For many seniors living outside the main districts, the closest PAWE is tens of kilometres away, essentially creating huge geographic deserts where the most vulnerable segments of the population are excluded from community support.
This geographic distance is a direct cause of a significant mobility barrier, a consequence of the combined factors of ageing, poor infrastructure, and financial constraints.
With age, normal deterioration in vision, motor reflexes, and chronic physical conditions often force older individuals to abandon driving and lose their independent mobility.
Public transportation options are sorely lacking in areas beyond major metropolitan transit networks.
Bus routes are sparse, real-time bus schedules are unavailable, and infrastructure is not barrier-free, including high steps on conventional buses and inaccessible walkways.

Private e-hailing services are an alternative in theory, but for low-income seniors who rely solely on fixed welfare assistance like JKM’s Bantuan Warga Emas (BWE), the transport costs incurred repeatedly are an out-of-pocket expense that is not sustainable.
Therefore, non-driving seniors depend on adult children or family members for regular transportation.

Seniors often opt out of attending activities at PAWE altogether, not wanting to be perceived as a domestic burden when working family members have demanding employment schedules or financial strains.
The federal government has tried to bridge the transport gaps through social assistance programs, especially through the Unit Penyayang Warga Emas (UPWE) run by JKM.

UPWE is a program that provides transport for senior citizens to access essential public services. UPWE has a small fleet of dedicated transport vehicles which are scattered all over Peninsular Malaysia.
However, these limited vehicles are overwhelmingly prioritised to transport frail or low-income seniors to essential medical appointments at public clinics and tertiary hospitals.
Daily transport for social, recreational and educational programs at PAWE centers remain almost entirely unserviced.

This institutional gap creates a self-reinforcing cycle of socio-spatial exclusion. Older adults are physically limited by distance and limited transport to their home environments and so their social networks shrink significantly with daily contact only occurring with members of their own household.
Research shows that this forced immobility accelerates cognitive decline, heightens feelings of loneliness and increases emotional distress.
Also, isolated seniors miss out on digital skills training available at PAWE facilities, leaving them behind in an increasingly digital world.

Policy experts are advocating for a complete reconfiguration of senior care delivery and age-friendly urban transit to dismantle these spatial and structural barriers before Malaysia achieves full aged nation status by 2040.

Instead of relying solely on centralised, stand-alone PAWE facilities, KPWKM and local district authorities should decentralise active ageing programs by establishing satellite micro-PAWE hubs in existing neighbourhood halls (dewan orang ramai) and deploying mobile activity vans to bring health and educational services directly into underserved rural villages.

At the same time, transportation accessibility should be improved by increasing UPWE vehicle fleet, establishing dedicated demand-responsive community shuttle services and mobilising local neighbourhood watch groups (Rukun Tetangga) to organise volunteer transit networks.

The easing of financial bottlenecks can be further improved with the extension of public transport concession schemes such as the Rapid Emas discount framework to subsidise targeted e-hailing fares for registered seniors travelling to activity centres.

Ultimately, incorporating senior mobility into transit-oriented urban planning will ensure that active ageing is not an exclusive privilege of urban dwellers but an achievable, equitable reality for all older Malaysians.

* Sayed Mohammad Reza Yamani Sayed Umar is a research fellow at the Ungku Aziz Centre for Development Studies (UAC), Universiti Malaya and Part-time Lecturer at Azman Hashim International Business School, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia. Author can be reached at smrezayamani@um.edu.my.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
ecd1ceb4a9459f2f: BRAGA, Nov 15 — Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark yesterday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football.
Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga.
The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures.
A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through while Portugal hope that yesterday’s disaster isn’t a sign of things to come.
“There are no nights to forget; it was a night of learning, of seeing the mistakes we made,” said Portugal midfielder Bruno Fernandes.
“Denmark were also very clinical — they scored from the chances they had and it was a match where things ultimately went wrong for us.”

Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys.
Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven.
Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches.

The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September.
Dominant Denmark

That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked like they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display.
Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute.

Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shell-shocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area.
Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent.
“Every single Denmark player put in their best performance I’ve seen in a long time. Even the substitutes, which made for a fantastic overall display,” said Morten Hjulmand.
“We scored some great goals and we deserved to win.”

Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time.

Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brooks’ chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B.

Northern Ireland meanwhile need a point from their final Group B2 match in Hungary on Tuesday to be promoted to League A for the first time after a 1-0 win over Ukraine secured by Terry Devlin’s first international goal. — AFP
4e62d870b6ac9361: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Barisan Nasional (BN) on the mandate given by the people of Melaka.
He expressed hope that the trust placed in BN would be discharged with full responsibility for the well-being of the state and its people.

“It is now time for us to move forward by prioritising the people’s interests, and the federal government will continue to strengthen cooperation with the Melaka state government to drive development and ensure the well-being of all the people,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to all voters who had fulfilled their democratic responsibility.
He extended similar appreciation to the Pakatan Harapan (PH) machinery and all its candidates for their hard work.
In the 16th Melaka State Election today, BN won 21 of the 28 seats to secure a two-thirds majority, while PH took four seats. — Bernama
d68cd603332252ab: PETALING JAYA: French president Emmanuel Macron’s two-day official visit to Malaysia, which starts tomorrow, will focus on diversifying France’s sources of rare earth supplies, which are essential for manufacturing electric motors and electronic devices.

In a post on X, Macron said his visits to Cambodia and Malaysia were aimed at strengthening economic partnerships and safeguarding jobs and industries in France and across the region, Bernama reported.

“In Malaysia, I am coming in particular to diversify our supplies of rare earths. We rarely talk about them, yet they are essential to making the magnets used in certain electric motors and electronic devices,” he said.
Macron said it would help French manufacturers reduce their vulnerability to supply chain disruptions by having multiple suppliers from different countries.

“For our factories, having several sources of supply means reducing the risk of having to shut down a production line for lack of parts. It also means being able to invest and produce in France with greater certainty about the future,” he added.
Macron also stressed on the need to form stronger international partnerships to ensure economic resilience and reduce dependence on limited sources of critical materials.
“More partners, less dependence. Our agreements open doors. Language, culture and friendship keep them open. That is good for our countries,” he said on X.
This will be Macron's second trip to Malaysia since 2017 but his first as president.
47909a571bfb6ecb: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to remain soft against the US dollar next week as the greenback remains well supported by expectations of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve (Fed).
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the greenback is expected to maintain its strength amid the Fed's hawkish monetary policy stance.

"Investor sentiment continues to favour the greenback amid expectations of a sizeable interest rate hike by the Fed in December. Market participants will also be closely monitoring the release of US retail sales data for October on Nov 17, with consensus estimates pointing to a 0.2 per cent month-on-month increase, compared with 0.8 per cent in September," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.10 against the US dollar next week.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit depreciated against the greenback to 4.0845/0890 from 4.0565/0610 a week earlier.
The local currency traded higher against a basket of other major currencies during the week.

It rose vis-à-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5549/5579 from 2.5616/5646 on the previous Friday, gained against the British pound to 5.4046/4106 from 5.4304/4365, and strengthened versus the euro to 4.5166/5216 from 4.5315/5365.
The ringgit also traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.

It increased against the Thai baht to 12.0611/0833 from 12.0898/1105 at the end of last week, rose vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.41/6.42 from 6.43/6.44, and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 224.3/224.6 from 224.2/224.6.
However, the local note eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1729/1769 from 3.1657/1694 a week earlier.
07ca7f573f42b2e2: WASHINGTON, Nov 15 — Tech giant Microsoft said yesterday it has “restored service” to customers, effectively drawing a close to a massive outage that caused chaos and disrupted public services and business around the world.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the US-based company said in an X post.

Microsoft had already reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating the major disruption was due to a technical issue and “not related to cyber or AI/agents.”

The outage swept the globe on Thursday, taking the company’s products offline in at least 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.
Microsoft had attributed the disruption to “elevated load” on its infrastructure.
It said the stoppage affected its Outlook email service, as well as Microsoft’s Teams communication platform and the company’s Copilot AI assistant.
Microsoft warned yesterday of an “active phishing campaign” to exploit the disruption, with fake emails imitating its service notifications.
The emails, detected on Friday, instructed users that messages blocked during the outage would be deleted if the recipient does not click to restore them. — AFP

54c9a9be79396b8a: KUALA LUMPUR: Bargain hunting is expected to emerge gradually on Bursa Malaysia next week as valuations become more attractive following a recent decline, according to Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng.
The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased to below 1,600 level in the last week and declined for five consecutive sessions, bringing it closer to oversold territory.
However, Thong anticipated the FBM KLCI to consolidate within the 1,580–1,600 range next week, with selective accumulation potentially supporting a technical rebound.
"While external uncertainties could continue to keep trading volatile, we expect bargain hunting to gradually emerge as valuations become more attractive," he told Bernama.
On key events next week, he said investors will monitor Malaysia's third quarter 2026 gross domestic product (GDP), October inflation and trade data for further indications of economic resilience.
He added that China's industrial production and retail sales figures as well as the US Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes will also influence regional sentiment.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FBM KLCI decreased 33.99 points to 1,582.59 from 1,616.58 a week earlier.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index slid 228.58 points to 11,736.89, the FBM Top 100 Index decreased 226.80 points to 11,571.65, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index trimmed 143.09 points to 11,679.68.
The FBM ACE Index slipped 177.10 points to 5,063.14 and the FBM Mid 70 Index tumbled 237.55 points to 16,783.33.

By sector, the Energy Index dropped 11.79 points to 783.07, the Plantation Index gained 69.71 points to 8,796.07, the Industrial Products and Services Index erased 1.26 points to 170.09, and the Financial Services Index weakened 444.86 points to 18,512.20.
Weekly turnover narrowed to 11.59 billion units worth RM7.70 billion from 15.49 billion units worth RM14.43 billion in the previous week.
The Main Market volume tumbled to 4.33 billion units valued at RM8.90 billion versus 8.30 billion units valued at RM13.08 billion previously.
Warrants turnover shrank to 3.27 billion units worth RM394.43 million against 5.23 billion units worth RM600.74 million a week ago.
However, the ACE Market volume increased to 2.60 billion units valued at RM734.92 million from 1.95 billion units valued at RM749.55 million in the preceding week.
a2fc5883aef7c997: DENVER: Fresh from a midterm election landslide, Democrats met in Denver this week united in wanting to deliver voters relief from high costs, but split over how to achieve that, what lessons to draw from their victory and how combative they should be toward President Donald Trump.

Despite the celebratory mood after the Nov 3 rout of Republicans, tensions between moderates and a restive progressive wing surfaced at the party's first major gathering since its victory, along with anxiety that the party could squander the opportunity voters had handed it.

The gathering offered an early glimpse of the battle to define its future as prospective 2028 presidential candidates and senior leaders debated how to turn electoral success into a governing agenda while navigating long-standing ideological and generational divides.

The conference, hosted by Majority Democrats, a group that advocates for younger party leaders and against left-wing activism, offered a forum for the jockeying now underway as Democrats debate what lessons to draw from their midterm win and begin the search for a 2028 White House standard-bearer.

Speakers disagreed over whether to embrace a bolder progressive agenda or tack toward the center, exposing competing approaches to lowering food, healthcare and housing costs, while working alongside Trump, who retains veto power for two more years.

California Representative Ro Khanna, a progressive and potential presidential candidate, urged Democrats to stop chasing the political center and embrace a bolder agenda, including universal healthcare, a wealth tax, a US$25 federal minimum wage, deep Pentagon cuts and abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

By contrast, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, a moderate and another potential 2028 contender, argued the party should move beyond ideological litmus tests, saying voters "don't give a damn" about such debates and care instead about whether Democrats can deliver results.
The breadth of the Democratic victories has allowed moderates and progressives to argue that voters have endorsed their vision for the party's future.

"It's to be expected that there will be a big debate because the Democratic victory was so broad it swept in centrists, southern Democrats and more progressive and left-wing Democrats," Democratic strategist Elaine Kamarck told Reuters.

Trump retains significant executive authority to block much of the Democrats' agenda, complicating the party's efforts to lower costs, the central issue voters gave Democrats control of Congress to fix.

Democrats are projected to hold at least 255 seats to ​Republicans' 169 in the US House, with 12 contests still ​undecided. In the Senate, the breakdown will be ⁠at least 55-44, with Democrats possibly gaining one more seat in Alaska when vote-counting is completed.
Work with Trump of fight him?
One of the most striking debates in Denver centered on how to govern with Trump still in the White House.
James Talarico, the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Texas since 1988, urged Democrats to work with Trump.

"We should make the final two years of his presidency the most productive of any presidency in American history," Talarico said, drawing tepid applause. "We're tired of being pitted against each other."
He found an ally in Iowa Governor-elect Rob Sand, who said he encouraged Democrats at campaign events to applaud Republicans and that partisan warfare will not deliver results.
"The only way we're going to fix that is by fixing it together," Sand said.
Minutes later, US Representative Jamie Raskin of Maryland and Eric Holder, who was attorney general in the Obama administration, largely rejected accommodation with Trump.

Raskin, expected to become chairman of the House Judiciary Committee in January and oversee investigations of Trump next year, said the Republican Party had become an authoritarian cult of personality.

"We're going to reassert all of the powers of Congress that have been surrendered and abdicated by the MAGA Congress to King Trump," Raskin said. "We're going to enforce the Constitution against him."
Holder warned Democrats against pursuing bipartisanship.

"If we retreat into caution, if we operate out of fear, if we take refuge in the niceties of the old Washington and seek approval from those who have been and are actively dismantling our institutions, we will fail."
There has been a long-simmering debate inside the party over whether to move further left or pursue a more centrist agenda, and this election has only intensified those tensions.
Competing visions for governing
Almost everyone who spoke at the conference agreed the party's top priority was lowering costs and improving life for working families.

It was a theme echoed by New York Representative Hakeem Jeffries, set to become US House Speaker, and several prospective 2028 presidential candidates, including Shapiro, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, and Khanna.
But splits emerged over how to achieve that.
Jeffries, a moderate, was heckled by a group of protesters, who accused him of being too timid to deliver change and called for a House leader who embraced a more populist progressive agenda.

Khanna and Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, another progressive who this week challenged more centrist Senator Chuck Schumer of New York for the party's top leadership job in the Senate, called for populist, government-funded economic solutions.
Don't blow it
There was a collective anxiety among the speakers that the party might squander one of the biggest victories it has achieved in a generation.
Many speakers described the win not as an enduring mandate, but rather a temporary opportunity voters had given them to fix the country's problems.
Arizona Senator Ruben Gallego, another potential presidential contender, noted that many Hispanic voters who voted for Trump in 2024 backed Democrats this month.
"It was not, though, a love letter to the Democratic Party," Gallego said. "It is a short-term loan that we need to keep paying, or we will lose it."
b86496903f4c638f: LOS ANGELES, Nov 15 — French Open winner Mirra Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 yesterday to book a WTA Finals title showdown with former champion Elina Svitolina in Indian Wells, California.

Ukraine’s Svitolina, who won the WTA Finals in 2018, fell to Ashleigh Barty in the final in the following year but hadn’t been back since, powered past Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-1 to give herself a shot at another triumph in the elite season-ending event.
“It’s really magical to be back in the finals,” Svitolina said. “Just very special for me to have this opportunity (Sunday), to have another battle another challenge.”
The 32-year-old, back in the top 10 this year for the first time since before her daughter, Skai, was born in 2022, will face a rising star in 19-year-old Andreeva.
The Russian teen won her maiden major at Roland Garros this year and with her victory over Pegula is assured of rising from third to second in the world rankings.
Andreeva remained unbeaten in her WTA Finals singles debut, having posted round robin victories over sixth-ranked Svitolina, world number two Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider.

She’s the youngest player to make the final since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 and joined Serena Williams and Chris Evert as the only players to win their first four matches in the event in straight sets.

“I think I can be very proud of myself,” she told Tennis Channel. “I’m very happy with how I’m playing. I’m very happy also with how I deal with the pressure. I knew this match had a lot on the line.”
For Pegula it was a match of missed chances, the fifth-ranked American unable to build on early breaks in both sets.
Andreeva double-faulted on break point to give Pegula a 2-1 lead in the opening set.
But the Russian broke back immediately, whipping a crosscourt forehand winner on her third break chance to make it 2-2.
Andreeva saved a pair of break points in the fifth game and broke again for a 5-3 lead.
Pegula had a chance to extend the set in the next game, but on break point she smashed what looked to be an easy backhand at the net past the baseline and Andreeva held to pocket the first.
Andreeva double-faulted to give Pegula a break chance in the fourth game of the second and the American converted for an imposing 3-1 lead.
But once again Andreeva broke back immediately, winning five of the last six games to close out the victory in one hour and 25 minutes.
Aggressive Svitolina
Svitolina said she did “pretty much everything” well against Noskova, who crumbled with 11 double faults as the Ukrainian surged to victory in just 65 minutes.
The Czech is second on the WTA Tour’s aces list behind Elena Rybakina but had just two — the second to save a match point in the penultimate game.
Noskova took the game, but it was a brief reprieve. In the next Svitolina took the match on her third match point when a Noskova forehand slid wide.
“I think I played really well today, serving good, returning well, too,” Svitolina said. “I was able to play aggressive and find the angles.”
The round robin format means Svitolina will have the chance, rare in tennis, of avenging her lopsided tomorrow loss to Andreeva in the same tournament.
“She’s in good form, but I feel like I’ve found my game since I lost the first match against her,” Svitolina said. “I will do my homework with my coaches and try to find the key.” — AFP

d0b24c21a1f6daa4: KYIV: Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in comments released Saturday, saying his country's relationship with the Western alliance is "back on the agenda."
Zelenskyy also warned of the dangers of Moscow's push to redraw "influence" in Europe and said the Kremlin was "betting everything" on this winter's military campaign.
Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Putin and Zelenskyy Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough.
Negotiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries would join future talks on ending the war.
In Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries – France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland – to send representatives to the talks.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelenskyy said, adding:
"After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go."
He said the discussion showed that "Nato is back on the agenda" for Ukraine.
Nato and Washington have not yet commented.

Russia meanwhile continued its bombardment on Saturday, with deadly strikes in the eastern city of Pavlohrad and in a village near Zaporizhzhia, which is now just a few dozen kilometres from the front line.
- KYIV SEEKS GUARANTEES -
Zelenskyy said Kyiv was discussing security guarantees with Western partners and that Ukrainians would ultimately decide whether to accept any deal.
He insisted Ukraine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow's troops as Russian.
Russia has consistently said Kyiv joining Nato is a red line and in 2022 launched its invasion, saying the West planned to incorporate Ukraine into the alliance.
The Kremlin has also ruled out foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine and wider ceasefires.
But Putin earlier this week proposed a "humanitarian" mission to the eastern town of Kostyantynivka, which Moscow announced it had seized in the summer but where Kyiv says fighting continues.
Zelenskyy said the proposal was a bid to advance Russian gains in Donetsk. "Their next steps will be our other cities in Donbas," he said.
Moscow's troops have inched westwards but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region.
- 'FIRST, END THE WAR' -
Russia has tried to reframe negotiations on ending the war – Europe's worst since World War II – into a conversation on the continent's wider security.
In 2021, before its Ukraine invasion, Moscow issued an ultimatum to the West to pull back Nato troops from eastern Europe.
Moscow's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, this week called for a "new, modern Yalta", drawing criticism from European leaders.
Zelenskyy warned that any discussion of wider security arrangements should come only after the war has ended.
European leaders have reacted coolly to the proposal for a new security architecture.
"We do not need to discuss that, it already exists," Germany's Friedrich Merz said Friday.
French President Emmanuel Macron said Saturday that "those who want to ration aid to Ukraine wish underneath it all to force an unjust peace on it" and, by extension, all of Europe.
"That is the spirit of defeat. That is a recipe for another war. That cannot be France's position," Macron said.
"What happens in Ukraine concerns us directly.... Helping Ukraine defend itself is protecting France and the French."
Donald Trump's administration has for almost two years tried to reach a breakthrough in talks between Russia and Ukraine. --AFP

083ec73521ecac57: MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has a full schedule at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits today, with the Myanmar crisis and South China Sea tensions expected to dominate discussions.

Anwar, who arrived on Saturday night, will attend the opening ceremony at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), where Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr will preside as Asean chair.
The summit plenary and leaders' retreat will follow.
Anwar is accompanied by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.

Later today, the prime minister will join fellow Asean leaders in separate meetings with representatives of the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth.
He is scheduled to receive a courtesy call from Asian Development Bank (ADB) president Masato Kanda in the evening.

The Foreign Ministry said the summit would give Malaysia an opportunity to exchange views on Asean Community building and the bloc's future direction, with talks focusing on strengthening regional resilience, energy security and supply chains amid shifting global conditions.
Leaders are expected to review the implementation of Asean's Five-Point Consensus (5PC) on Myanmar and discuss the bloc's next steps.
Maritime security talks are expected to cover the proposed establishment of an Asean Maritime Centre and progress in negotiations on a South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC).
The ministry said leaders were also expected to discuss transboundary haze pollution and the ongoing crisis in Middle East.
On Monday, Anwar is scheduled to attend summits with China, Australia, South Korea and the United Nations.

The three-day gathering, themed "Navigating Our Future, Together", will conclude on Tuesday with further meetings, including the Asean-United States Special Summit, and the handover of the Asean chairmanship from the Philippines to Singapore.

6c7cbaa99cf5f281: PETALING JAYA: Membanteras perdagangan haram memerlukan kerajaan menangani kelemahan sistemik secara menyeluruh, kata pakar.

Presiden Transparency International Malaysia (TI-Malaysia), Raymon Ram, berkata perdagangan haram bukan sekadar isu kehilangan hasil negara, tetapi juga persoalan integriti institusi, rasuah dan jenayah terancang.
Beliau berkata demikian ketika mengulas dapatan Transnational Alliance to Combat Illicit Trade dalam laporan 'Menilai Prestasi Asean dalam Indeks Perdagangan Haram' bagi tahun 2025.

Walaupun Malaysia meraih markah tinggi sebanyak 77.3 daripada 100 mata bagi aspek perdagangan, kastam dan kawalan sempadan, skor negara menjunam kepada 24.7 mata bagi pengawasan terhadap perniagaan tempatan seperti pengendali gudang serta pasaran dalam talian.
Raymon berkata, kelemahan itu mencerminkan jurang antara kewujudan undang-undang dengan keberkesanan penguatkuasaannya.
"Walaupun kawalan sempadan Malaysia mencatatkan skor yang baik, pengawasan terhadap gudang, pengedar dan platform dalam talian masih lemah," katanya.
"Lebih membimbangkan, kegiatan perdagangan haram turut membuka ruang kepada rasuah, penyalahgunaan kuasa dan kemungkinan wujudnya perlindungan terhadap sindiket."
Raymon berhujah, kerajaan perlu memperkukuh kawalan dalaman, audit berasaskan risiko dan pengesanan keseluruhan rantaian bekalan, katanya.
Malaysia juga memerlukan penyelarasan penguatkuasaan yang lebih berstruktur, dengan perkongsian risikan, tanggungjawab yang jelas dan sasaran prestasi bersama, katanya.
"Kejayaan penguatkuasaan tidak boleh diukur melalui nilai rampasan semata-mata, tetapi sejauh mana dalang, pembiaya dan pihak yang bersekongkol berjaya dibawa ke muka pengadilan.
"Yang diperlukan ialah tindakan bersepadu yang mampu memutuskan keseluruhan rangkaian penyeludupan, bukan sekadar menangkap pengedar atau merampas barangan," katanya.
Pakar kriminologi, Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid, berkata persoalan yang lazim timbul apabila bercakap hal perdagangan haram adalah sejauh mana undang-undang dilaksanakan dan keberkesanan pantauan.
"Perdagangan haram melibatkan satu rangkaian, daripada pembekal, penyimpanan, pengedaran sampailah kepada penjualan kepada pengguna," katanya.
Pensyarah kanan di Fakulti Undang-undang Universiti Malaya ini berkata, penyelarasan dan perkongsian maklumat antara agensi sangat penting untuk tindakan penguatkuasaan yang menyeluruh.
"Kita perlu lihat siapa sebenarnya di belakang kegiatan ini, siapa pembekal, siapa pengedar dan siapa yang mendapat keuntungan," katanya.
Beliau juga menyeru pemantauan terhadap platform dalam talian diperkukuhkan.
Katanya, platform perlu ada tanggungjawab memastikan penjual dan barangan yang ditawarkan tidak melanggar undang-undang.
"Kalau iklan diturunkan atau akaun ditutup tetapi penjual boleh buka akaun baharu dan teruskan kegiatan yang sama, masalah sebenarnya masih tidak selesai," katanya.

Hazmi Mohd Rusli, pakar undang-undang laut antarabangsa di Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia berkata, Malaysia sebenarnya mempunyai peruntukan undang-undang yang boleh digunakan untuk menangani perdagangan haram.

"Cabarannya adalah dari segi pelaksanaan dan pemantauan, khususnya yang melibatkan platform dalam talian. Identiti penjual perlu disahkan dengan lebih teliti bagi memastikan barangan haram tidak mudah dijual secara terbuka," katanya.
Katanya lagi, tindakan penguatkuasaan perlu dilaksanakan secara berterusan dan bukan hanya apabila terdapat aduan atau ketika operasi besar-besaran dijalankan.
64b798eab5369eee: TELUK INTAN: When the Kinta River begins to rise during the rainy season, Anuar Osman knows there is little time to waste.
For about a week, schools of "lundu" - a type of catfish - move through the river in large numbers, creating a short but lucrative fishing season for those who know where to place their traps.

Anuar, 49, is an inland fisherman who also manages an oil palm smallholding. Catching lundu is not his main livelihood but, when the river swells, the opportunity can be hard to ignore: on a good day, catches can exceed 100kg.
“When we see the water rising, we have to quickly set the 'belat' because the fish only come in for about a week,” he said, noting that they "retire" from catching them once the river drops.
The belat, a traditional fish trap positioned along the river’s course, is particularly suited to lundu. The fish have sharp spines, making them difficult to remove from nets once they get entangled.
Another inland fisherman, Shahril Yeop Mat Sibi, 37, said the lundu appear to move from the lower reaches of the Perak River into the Kinta River when water levels rise.
The traps do not require bait: instead, the fish move in schools with the current and enter the belat placed strategically along the riverbanks.
“As long as the belat is not full, the fish will keep entering,” Shahril, who also works in a school canteen, explained.
“Once it fills, we bring it up quickly because more fish from downstream will continue moving upstream.”
For fishermen who understand the river’s seasonal rhythms, the brief migration can provide significant extra income.
Trader Jasnurol Iznal Zainal Abidin, 43, said he sells between 300kg and 600kg of lundu a day during the season at around RM30 per kg, depending on supply.
His biggest haul came last year, when he sold about two tonnes in a single day.
But the river’s bounty comes with risks. Crocodiles are known to inhabit the area, while rising water also means stronger currents and more unpredictable conditions.
Jasnurol cautioned fishermen not to underestimate the river, particularly when checking traps during periods of high water.
For experienced folks such as Anuar and Shahril, however, the signs are familiar: the river rises, the lundu arrive, the traps are set - and the season is on.
39994499436d36ce: Drawing upon Lord Denning’s advocacy of common sense in judicial decisions – alongside my own worldly and judicial experience in Malaysia, rooted in my origins in Thopputhurai, Vedaranyam, Tamil Nadu, India – I will state bluntly: no person operating in isolation possesses the capacity to defraud a nation on a scale that attracts universal infamy without the active assistance of a wider network.

When I sat as a judge, I treated common sense as my primary guiding principle when interpreting the Federal Constitution, the law and the facts of any case. It was strictly through this practical approach that I developed the oath of office jurisprudence as well as the concept of university-cum-court annexed arbitration.

With his 38-year career on the English bench, Denning earned the title of “the people’s judge”. At the heart of his jurisprudence was a simple, powerful conviction: the law is neither an abstract puzzle for academics nor a rigid trap for ordinary citizens.
Instead, he advocated, judges and lawyers must apply practical common sense to achieve real justice when interpreting both statutes and facts.
Among his many judgments grounded in common sense, I was particularly guided by his approach in Butler Machine Tool Co Ltd v Ex-Cell-O Corp (England) Ltd.

In resolving commercial contract disputes, Denning advocated looking at the entirety of the documents to determine what a sensible businessperson would understand, rather than applying rigid, artificial formulas.

Regarding the SRC International case, I have previously written that, among other critical issues, Najib Razak was deprived of procedural fairness and his constitutional right to counsel. Common sense dictates that procedural fairness is a core pillar of the criminal justice system and our constitutional framework.

Furthermore, it is a fallacy for certain commentators to circulate articles suggesting that a single Malay individual could orchestrate a massive fraud against the nation entirely on his own without the involvement of non-Malay enablers and professionals.

In my view, it is a travesty of justice to paint a picture suggesting that one person possessed the solitary capability to execute a grand-scale national scam without the active participation of accomplices across different communities.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
b8d06d0ac0308c80: NEW YORK: Elon Musk's SpaceX on Saturday pulled off the first-ever "catch" of a spaceship, a technical feat that shows the feasibility of fully reusable rockets and brings affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality.

The Starship emerged from a cloudy sky after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth's atmosphere, then descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical "chopstick arms" above Launch Pad 2.

The success marked a milestone in the space industry's decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems -- a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible.
"That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes," SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said.

Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with 1977 soft rock hit "Baby Come Back" serving as the soundtrack of the nerve-wracking final descent on SpaceX's official livestream.
It was the 15th test flight of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket system.
The Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk's Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.

Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the "catch" of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude compared to boosters.
Musk congratulated the SpaceX team and posted videos of the spaceship hanging between the chopstick arms, saying the vessel "looks great!"

Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a "huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work."
"Let's see how quickly they can do it again," he added.
Analyst Kathleen Curlee hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done.

"What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability... to handle sensitive payloads and missions," said Curlee, of Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology.
Giant swoosh
Starship's path home had been carefully mapped out to avoid population centers as it traveled over the continent, said senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore.

Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a "giant swoosh maneuver" in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas' Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east.
Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars.
US space agency Nasa is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman called the spaceship recovery "almost magic."
"Making more believers by the day... one step closer to (the Moon)," he said on X.
Musk envisions Starship as being the workhorse of "rapidly reusable" rockets, with a goal of hourly launches that could send things like internet satellites and data centers into space.
Refueling challenge

Musk, the world's richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which regularly launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station.

But the Starship project has been plagued by delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges, including the unsolved problem of transferring fuel to the spaceship while in orbit -- a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars.

It will also need to further fine-tune the Super Heavy booster, which ran into a technical issue Friday on its descent, forcing a diversion to the Gulf of Mexico. It, too, was supposed to have been caught by the "chopstick arms."
Following SpaceX's high-profile stock market debut in June that raised about US$85.7 billion, the company is investing heavily in production and launch capabilities.

During a tour of its million-square-foot (93,000-square-meter) factory at Starbase on Friday, SpaceX officials told journalists it now has the capability to produce a spaceship every two weeks and a booster every four weeks.

11d3bd4b8a2557f4: LOS ANGELES: Aryna Sabalenka apologized on Saturday after an on-court outburst during her defeat to Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

"I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online," Sabalenka wrote in a post on Instagram.
